title.zh: 卷四百 列傳第一百五十九 王信 汪大猷 袁燮 吳柔勝 游仲鴻 李祥 王介 宋德之 楊大全
title.en: Volume 400 Biographies 159: Wang Xin, Wang Dayou, Yuan Xie, Wu Rousheng, You Zhonghong, Li Xiang, Wang Jie, Song Dezhi, Yang Daquan
title.raw: 卷四百 列傳第一百五十九 王信 汪大猷 袁燮 吳柔勝 游仲鴻 李祥 王介 宋德之 楊大全 Volume 400 Biographies 159: Wang Xin, Wang Dayou, Yuan Xie, Wu Rousheng, You Zhonghong, Li Xiang, Wang Jie, Song Dezhi, Yang Daquan

sentences.zh: 王信，字誠之，處州麗水人。

translations.literal: Wang Xin, style name Chengzhi, was a native of Lishui in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin, whose courtesy name was Chengzhi, came from Lishui in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 既冠，入太學，登紹興三十年進士第，試中教官，授建康府學教授。

translations.literal: After he came of age he entered the Imperial University, passed the jinshi examination in the thirtieth year of Shaoxing, qualified in the instructor examination, and was appointed professor at the Jiankang Prefecture school.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had reached manhood, he entered the Imperial University, took his jinshi degree in the thirtieth year of the Shaoxing reign, passed the examination for instructors, and was made professor at the Jiankang prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，進所著《唐太宗論讚》及《負薪論》，孝宗覽之，嘉歎不已，特循兩資，授太學博士。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning; when the mourning ended he presented his works "Commentary and Praise on Emperor Taizong of Tang" and "On Carrying Firewood"; Emperor Xiaozong read them, praised them without cease, specially advanced him two ranks, and appointed him Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he completed the mourning period and submitted his "Commentary and Praise on Emperor Taizong of Tang" and his "On Carrying Firewood." Xiaozong read them and marveled; he specially advanced Xin two ranks and appointed him Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時須次者例徙外，添差溫州教授。

translations.literal: At that time those awaiting their turn in the queue were routinely transferred outward; he was given an additional assignment as professor at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Those waiting their turn for appointment were routinely sent to posts outside the capital; Xin received an additional assignment as professor at Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 郡饑疫，議遣官振救之，父老願得信任其事，守不欲以煩信，請益力，信聞之，欣然為行，遍至病者家，全活不可勝記。

translations.literal: The prefecture suffered famine and pestilence; officials discussed sending someone to bring relief; the elders wished to have Wang Xin take charge of the matter; the prefect did not wish to trouble Xin, but they pressed harder; when Xin heard of it he gladly undertook the mission, went to every household with the sick, and saved lives beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When famine and plague struck the prefecture, the authorities debated dispatching an official to provide relief. The local elders asked that Wang Xin be entrusted with the task. The prefect was reluctant to burden him, but they pressed their request; when Xin heard of it he set out gladly, visited every afflicted household in turn, and saved more lives than could be recorded.

sentences.zh: 差敕令所刪定官，法令有不合人情，自相牴牾，吏得以傅會出入者，悉𨤲正之。

translations.literal: He was assigned as reviser at the Statutes and Ordinances Office; wherever laws were at odds with human feeling, contradicted one another, or allowed clerks to twist them for personal advantage, he corrected them all.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned as a reviser at the Statutes and Ordinances Office, he corrected every regulation that failed to accord with human feeling, contradicted another rule, or gave clerks room to manipulate outcomes for their own gain.

sentences.zh: 轉對，言：「敵情不可測，和議不可恃，今日要當先為自備之策，以待可乘之機。

translations.literal: At a court audience he said: "The enemy's intentions cannot be foreseen, and the peace agreement cannot be relied upon; what is essential today is first to prepare measures of self-defense and await an opportunity that may be seized."
translations.idiomatic: Presenting himself at court, he said, "The enemy's intentions cannot be predicted, and the peace agreement cannot be trusted. What matters now is to prepare for self-defense first and wait for a chance that may be seized."

sentences.zh: 」上以為是。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded this as correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又論：「太學正、錄掌規矩之官而員多，博士掌訓導之官而員少，請以正、錄兩員升為博士。

translations.literal: He also argued: "The Rectors and Recorders of the Imperial University hold posts that enforce regulations yet are numerous, while the Erudites who direct instruction are few; I ask that two posts of Rector and Recorder be promoted to Erudite."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the university had too many Rectors and Recorders—officers charged with enforcing rules—and too few Erudites to guide instruction, and proposed promoting two Rectors or Recorders to Erudite posts.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The court approved it.
translations.idiomatic: His proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 論除官脞冗之敝，乞精選監司而擇籍名，郡將代半歲乃注人。

translations.literal: He discussed the abuse of redundant appointments in making dismissals, begged that supervisory commissioners be carefully selected and rosters chosen, and that prefects be replaced only after half a year before new men were registered.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized the bloated practice of making appointments and dismissals, urged that circuit supervisors be chosen with care from named rosters, and that new prefects not be registered until their predecessors had served half a year.

sentences.zh: 上親以其章授宰臣行。

translations.literal: The emperor personally handed his memorial to the chief ministers for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally handed his memorial to the chief ministers with orders to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 權考功郎官。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Merit and Demerit Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Merit and Demerit Section.

sentences.zh: 蜀人張公遷，初八年免銓，至是改秩，吏妄引言，復令柅之，信鉤考其故，吏怖服。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongqian of Shu, who at first had been exempted from the roster review for eight years, was now changing rank; a clerk falsely cited a precedent and again blocked him; Xin investigated the reason and the clerk submitted in fear.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu native named Zhang Gongqian had first been exempted from roster review for eight years and was now due for a rank change; a clerk falsely cited precedent to block him again. Xin traced the matter and the clerk confessed in terror.

sentences.zh: 有三蜀士實礙式，吏受賕為地，工部尚書趙雄，蜀人也，以屬信，信持弗聽，已而轉吏部閱審成牘，撫掌愧歎，嗟激不已，以聞於上。

translations.literal: Three scholars from Shu were in fact impeded by formal requirements; a clerk had accepted a bribe to make room for them; Minister of Works Zhao Xiong, himself a man of Shu, interceded with Xin, but Xin would not listen; later, when he transferred to the Ministry of Personnel to review completed dossiers, he clapped his hands in shame and sighed with emotion without end, and reported the matter to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Three Shu scholars were genuinely blocked by formal requirements while a clerk took bribes to clear a path for others. Zhao Xiong of the Ministry of Works, himself from Shu, asked Xin to yield, but Xin refused. Later, reviewing completed dossiers in the Ministry of Personnel, he clapped his hands in dismay, sighed again and again, and reported the affair to the throne.

sentences.zh: 它日，上謂尚書蔡洸曰：「考功得王信，銓曹遂清。

translations.literal: Another day, the Emperor said to Cai Guang, Minister of the Secretariat: "Now that the Department of Evaluation has obtained Wang Xin, the Bureau of Appointments has been cleared."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, the Emperor said to Cai Guang, Minister of the Secretariat, "With Wang Xin in the Department of Evaluation, the Bureau of Appointments is finally clean."

sentences.zh: 」邏者私相語，指為神明。

translations.literal: Those who heard it spoke privately among themselves, pointing to him as a divine being.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread quietly among officials, who hailed him as practically a god.

sentences.zh: 武臣給告不書年齒，磨轉蔭薦，肆為姦欺，不可控搏，為擿最者數事告宰相，付之大理獄。

translations.literal: Military officers on leave did not record their ages; through rotation and hereditary privilege recommendations they committed brazen fraud that could not be restrained. He selected several of the worst cases, reported them to the Grand Councillor, and had them handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers omitted their ages on leave requests and abused rotation and hereditary privilege to commit fraud so brazen it could not be checked. Wang Xin singled out the worst abuses, reported them to the Grand Councillor, and saw the offenders sent to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 事連三衙，殿帥王友直銳爭之，上審知其非，沮之曰：「考功所言，公事也，汝將何為？

translations.literal: The affair implicated the Three Yamen, and Wang Youzhi, the Hall commander, forcefully contested it. The Emperor, knowing they were in the wrong, checked them and said: "What the Department of Evaluation speaks of is public business—what do you intend to do?"
translations.idiomatic: The case touched the Three Yamen, and Hall Commander Wang Youzhi fought it fiercely. The Emperor knew they were wrong and cut them off: "The Department of Evaluation is speaking of official business—what are you going to do about it?"

sentences.zh: 」獄具，皆伏辜。

translations.literal: When the trial was concluded, all confessed their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the trial concluded, all confessed their crimes.

sentences.zh: 因請置籍，以柅後患。

translations.literal: He therefore requested that registers be established to check future abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked that registers be kept to guard against future abuses.

sentences.zh: 授軍器少監，仍兼考功郎官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Armory, while still concurrently serving as an official of the Department of Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Armory while retaining his post in the Department of Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，吏裒金殺牲禱神，願信服闋無再為考功。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, clerks collected money and slaughtered animals to pray to the gods, expressing the wish that after his mourning ended he would never again serve in the Department of Evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother, clerks pooled money and sacrificed animals to the gods, praying that once his mourning ended he would never return to the Department of Evaluation.

sentences.zh: 既起，知永州。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, he was appointed prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was appointed prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 入奏事，留為將作少監，復考功郎官，轉軍器少監兼右司郎官，升員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered to report on affairs and was retained as Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, again as an official of the Department of Evaluation; he was transferred to Vice Director of the Armory concurrently as an official of the Right Bureau, and promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Called in to report on affairs, he was kept at court as Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and again as an official of the Department of Evaluation; he then moved to Vice Director of the Armory with a concurrent post in the Right Bureau, and was promoted to Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 四方有以疑獄來上者，信反復披覽，常至夜分。

translations.literal: When doubtful legal cases came from all quarters, Wang Xin repeatedly examined them, often until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever knotty cases arrived from across the realm, Wang Xin read through them again and again, often working past midnight.

sentences.zh: 升左司員外郎，轉對，論士大夫趨向之敝：「居官者逃一時之責，而後之禍患有所不恤；

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Director of the Left Bureau, he spoke in audience on the abuses in the inclinations of scholar-officials: "Those in office evade immediate responsibility, yet give no thought to later calamities;"
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Director of the Left Bureau, he addressed the throne on the failings of the scholar-official class: "Officeholders dodge present accountability and give no thought to the disasters that follow;"

sentences.zh: 獻言者求一時之合，而行之可否有所不計。

translations.literal: "Those who offer advice seek momentary agreement, without considering whether implementation is feasible;"
translations.idiomatic: "Advisers chase momentary approval and never weigh whether a policy can actually be carried out;"

sentences.zh: 集事者以趣辦為能，而不為根本之慮；

translations.literal: "Those who gather affairs treat quick completion as ability, without concern for fundamental considerations;"
translations.idiomatic: "Men who rush business treat speed as competence and never look to the root of things;"

sentences.zh: 謀利者以羨餘為事，而不究源流之實。

translations.literal: "Those who seek profit take surplus as their business, without investigating the true source and flow."
translations.idiomatic: "Those who chase profit fix on whatever margin remains and never trace matters to their source."

sentences.zh: 持論尚刻薄，而寖失祖宗忠厚之意；

translations.literal: "Arguments tend toward harshness, gradually losing the generous integrity of the founding ancestors;"
translations.idiomatic: "Debate grows ever harsher, and by degrees the generous spirit of the founding ancestors is lost;"

sentences.zh: 革敝預煩碎，而不明國家寬大之體。

translations.literal: "Reform of abuses anticipates fussy minutiae, without clarifying the magnanimous character of the state."
translations.idiomatic: "Reform piles up petty detail and never makes clear the broad, generous body of the state."

sentences.zh: 因循玩習，恬不為怪。

translations.literal: Following old ways and treating them as habit, one is calmly not surprised.
translations.idiomatic: Custom is followed and habit indulged until none think it strange.

sentences.zh: 願酌古之道，當時之宜，示好惡於取舍之間，使天下靡然知鄉，而無復為目前苟且之徇。

translations.literal: "May Your Majesty weigh the way of antiquity and the needs of the present, show likes and dislikes in what is chosen and rejected, so that all under Heaven naturally know the direction, and no longer follow present expediency."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask that Your Majesty weigh the ways of antiquity against the needs of the age, make clear what you favor and what you reject, and lead the realm to move as one—so that no one again serves only the convenience of the moment."

sentences.zh: 」又論：「朝廷有恤民之政，而州縣不能行恤民之實。

translations.literal: He also argued: "The court has policies to care for the people, yet prefectures and counties cannot carry out the substance of caring for the people."
translations.idiomatic: He went on: "The court has policies meant to relieve the people, but the prefectures and counties never deliver real relief."

sentences.zh: 近歲不登，陛下軫念元元，凡水旱州郡租賦，或蠲放，或倚閣住催。

translations.literal: In recent years harvests have failed. Your Majesty, compassionate toward the common people, ordered that in all flood- and drought-stricken prefectures and commanderies, rent and tax be either remitted or deferred with collection suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Harvests have failed in recent years, and Your Majesty, moved by the plight of the people, ordered that in every flood- or drought-stricken command, rents and taxes be either remitted outright or deferred with collection halted.

sentences.zh: 然倚閣住催之名可以並緣為擾，願明與減放。

translations.literal: Yet the name of deferring collection can be exploited together as harassment; I wish that remission be made explicit and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the label of deferred collection gives local officials room to harass the people on the side; I ask that reductions and remissions be stated plainly.

sentences.zh: 」又論豫備三說：收逃亡之卒，選忠順之官，嚴訓練之職。

translations.literal: He also discussed three points on advance preparation: reclaim fugitive soldiers, select loyal and obedient officials, and tighten the duties of training.
translations.idiomatic: He also set out three measures of preparedness: reclaim deserters, appoint loyal and dependable officials, and enforce military training.

sentences.zh: 又言屯田利害。

translations.literal: He also spoke on the advantages and disadvantages of military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed the costs and benefits of frontier garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 上皆納其說。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted everything he proposed.

sentences.zh: 兼玉牒所檢討官、提領戶部酒庫。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as reviser of the Imperial Genealogy Office and overseer of the Ministry of Revenue's wine treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He also held concurrent posts as reviser of the Imperial Genealogy Office and superintendent of the Ministry of Revenue's wine monopoly stores.

sentences.zh: 久之，上諭信曰：「知朕意否？

translations.literal: After some time, the Emperor told Wang Xin: "Do you know my intention?"
translations.idiomatic: After a time, the Emperor said to Wang Xin, "Do you understand what I have in mind?"

sentences.zh: 行用卿，慮書生不長於財賦，故以命卿，果能副朕所委。」

translations.literal: "I am about to employ you; concerned that scholars are not skilled in finance and taxation, I therefore assigned you this duty—you have indeed fulfilled what I entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: "I mean to put you to use. I worried that a man of letters would not excel at revenue and finance, so I gave you this charge—and you have truly lived up to what I asked."

sentences.zh: 為中書門下檢正諸房文字，遷太常少卿兼權中書舍人。

translations.literal: He served as rectifier of documents for the various sections of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship, concurrently acting as Secretariat Drafting Official.
translations.idiomatic: He served as rectifier of documents in the Secretariat-Chancellery, then was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship with concurrent duty as Acting Secretariat Drafting Official.

sentences.zh: 假禮部尚書使於金，肄射都亭，連中其的，金人駴曰：「尚書得非黑王相公子孫耶？

translations.literal: Temporarily appointed Minister of Rites on a mission to the Jin, he practiced archery at the Capital Pavilion and hit the target in succession. The Jin people were startled and said: "Is the Minister not a descendant of Prime Minister Black Wang?"
translations.idiomatic: Sent to the Jin as Acting Minister of Rites, he practiced archery at the Capital Pavilion and hit the mark again and again. The Jurchens cried out in astonishment: "Surely this minister is kin to Prime Minister Black Wang!"

sentences.zh: 」謂王德用也。

translations.literal: They meant Wang Deyong.
translations.idiomatic: They meant Wang Deyong.

sentences.zh: 信得米芾書法，金人寶之。

translations.literal: Wang Xin possessed Mi Fu's calligraphy; the Jin people treasured it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin owned calligraphy by Mi Fu, which the Jurchens prized.

sentences.zh: 歸言金人必衰之兆有四，在我當備之策有二，上首肯之。

translations.literal: Upon returning, he reported four omens that the Jin would inevitably decline and two policies that the Song ought to prepare; the Emperor nodded in assent.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported four signs that the Jin must decline and two measures the Song should ready; the Emperor nodded his agreement.

sentences.zh: 太史奏仲秋日月五星會於軫，信言：「休咎之徵，史策不同，然五星聚者有之，未聞七政共集也。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer reported that in mid-autumn the sun, moon, and five planets would converge at the asterism Zhen. Wang Xin said: "Portents of fortune and calamity differ in the historical records; though gatherings of five planets are recorded, I have never heard of all seven luminaries gathering together."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer announced that at mid-autumn the sun, moon, and five planets would meet in the asterism Zhen. Wang Xin said: "Records disagree on whether such signs bring blessing or disaster; gatherings of five planets appear in the histories, but never all seven luminaries at once."

sentences.zh: 分野在楚，願思所以順天而應之。

translations.literal: "The corresponding territory is Chu; I hope Your Majesty will consider how to comply with Heaven and respond to it."
translations.idiomatic: "The region affected is Chu. I ask Your Majesty to consider how to align with Heaven and answer this sign."

sentences.zh: 」因條上七事。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a list of seven items.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial listing seven measures.

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下即位之初，經營中原之志甚銳，然功之所以未立者，正以所用之人不一。

translations.literal: He also said: "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, your resolve to recover the Central Plains was very sharp; yet the reason achievement has not been realized is precisely that those employed are not unified."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, your will to recover the Central Plains burned bright; yet the reason success has not come is simply that the men you rely on are not of one mind."

sentences.zh: 其人不一，故其論不一；

translations.literal: If the people are not unified, their opinions are not unified;
translations.idiomatic: When the men are not one, their counsel is not one;

sentences.zh: 其論不一，故其心不一。

translations.literal: if their opinions are not unified, their hearts are not unified.
translations.idiomatic: when their counsel is not one, their hearts are not one.

sentences.zh: 願豫求至當之論，使歸於一。

translations.literal: I wish that you seek the most appropriate policy in advance, bringing all to unity.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty settle on the right course beforehand and bring every voice to a single purpose.

sentences.zh: 鎖闈封駁，而右府所不下關中書，或斜封捷出，左於公論。

translations.literal: Sealed examination halls with sealed rejections—yet what the Right Secretariat fails to send through the Secretariat-Chancellery sometimes slips out through irregular seals, contrary to public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations are sealed and rejections sealed in return—yet what the Right Secretariat withholds from the central office sometimes escapes through improper seals, against the judgment of the court.

sentences.zh: 統領官奴事內侍，坐謫遠州，幸蒙赦還而遽復故職。

translations.literal: Commanding officers who enslaved themselves to inner eunuchs were demoted to distant prefectures; after fortunately receiving amnesty and returning, they were immediately restored to their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Field commanders who had become the creatures of palace eunuchs were banished to remote posts; pardoned and brought back, they were at once restored to their old ranks.

sentences.zh: 潛藩恩舊之隸徒，榷酤官而齒朝士。

translations.literal: Bondservants who were old favorites from when the Emperor was in his princely residence hold monopoly liquor offices yet rank alongside court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Servants who had been favorites in the Emperor's days as heir now hold liquor monopoly posts and sit in rank beside court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 老禁校僥冀節鉞，詭計可得之，而奉稍恩典，與正不異。

translations.literal: Veteran palace guards hope for frontier commands through devious schemes, yet their salary and privileges differ little from regular appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Old guards of the inner palace angle for military commissions by crooked means, yet their pay and perquisites differ scarcely at all from those of regular appointees.

sentences.zh: 閤門多溢額祗候。

translations.literal: The Gatehouse has many supernumerary attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Gatehouse is crowded with attendants beyond the authorized quota.

sentences.zh: 妃嬪進封而冒指它姓為甥侄。

translations.literal: Imperial consorts, upon advancement in rank, falsely claim people of other surnames as nephews and nieces.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial consorts are promoted in rank, they falsely claim outsiders as nephews and nieces.

sentences.zh: 既一一塗歸，有雖書讀而徐核其不當者，續爭救之。

translations.literal: Having corrected each one in turn, when there were cases where even though the memorial was read he slowly verified what was improper, he continued to argue and remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: He corrected each abuse in turn; and when a memorial had already been read, he still went back, examined what was wrong, and fought to block it.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「事有不可不問者，第言之，朕無有不為卿行者。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Matters that must be investigated—just speak of them; there is nothing I would not do for you."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "If something must be looked into, say so. There is nothing I will not do for you."

sentences.zh: 」於是益抗志不回。

translations.literal: Thereupon he became even more resolute and unyielding in purpose.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he grew only bolder and more unbending.

sentences.zh: 宦者甘昪既逐遠之矣，屬高宗崩，用治喪事，人莫敢言。

translations.literal: The eunuch Gan Sheng had already been banished to a distance; when Gaozong died, he was employed for funeral affairs, and no one dared speak about it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Gan Sheng had already been sent far away; when Gaozong died, he was put in charge of the funeral, and no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 俄提舉德壽宮，信亟執奏，舉朝皆悚。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed superintendent of De Shou Palace; Wang Xin urgently submitted a memorial, and the entire court was shocked.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gan Sheng was appointed superintendent of De Shou Palace. Wang Xin immediately memorialized against it, and the whole court trembled.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士洪邁適入，上語之曰：「王給事論甘昪事甚當。

translations.literal: The Hanlin Academician Hong Mai happened to enter; the Emperor told him: "Remonstrating Official Wang's argument on the Gan Sheng matter is very apt."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Hong Mai happened to arrive; the Emperor told him, "Supervising Secretary Wang's protest over Gan Sheng is entirely right."

sentences.zh: 朕特白太上皇后，聖訓以為：『今一宮之事異於向時，非我老人所能任，小黃門空多，類不習事，獨昪可任責，分吾憂。

translations.literal: I specially informed the Retired Empress; her sacred instruction was: "Affairs of the palace today differ from former times—not something this old person can manage. The junior eunuchs are many but mostly inexperienced; only Sheng can bear responsibility and share my cares."
translations.idiomatic: I spoke specially to the Retired Empress. Her instruction was: "Palace affairs today are not what they once were; an old woman like me cannot manage them. The junior eunuchs are numerous and mostly know nothing of business—only Sheng can take responsibility and share my burden."

sentences.zh: 渠今已歸，居室尚不能有，豈敢蹈故態。

translations.literal: "He has now returned, yet cannot even have a dwelling—how would he dare repeat his former conduct?"
translations.idiomatic: "He has come back and still lacks a proper home—how would he dare fall into his old ways?"

sentences.zh: 』以是駁疏不欲行。

translations.literal: For this reason the Emperor rejected the memorial and did not wish to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: On that ground the Emperor rejected the memorial and refused to act on it.

sentences.zh: 卿見王給事，可道此意。

translations.literal: When you see Remonstrating Official Wang, you may convey this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When you see Supervising Secretary Wang, tell him what I have said.

sentences.zh: 」信聞之乃止。

translations.literal: Wang Xin heard this and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xin heard this, he desisted.

sentences.zh: 信遇事剛果，論奏不避權要，繇此人多嫉之，信亦力求去，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: Wang Xin was firm and decisive in handling affairs; in memorials he did not avoid the powerful, and for this many envied him. Wang Xin also strenuously sought to leave office and was appointed to oversee Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin was bold and resolute in action; in memorials he never shrank from the powerful, and many came to resent him for it. He pressed hard to leave office and was appointed superintendent of Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 詔求言，信條十事以獻，其目曰：法戒輕變，令貴必行，寬州郡以養民力，修軍政以待機會，郡當分其緩急，縣當別其劇易，嚴銅錢之禁，廣積聚之備，處歸附之人，收逃亡之卒。

translations.literal: An edict sought advice; Wang Xin listed ten items to present, their headings: laws should guard against rash change; orders should value certain execution; relax prefectures and commanderies to nurture popular strength; revise military administration to await opportunity; commanderies should distinguish urgency and delay; counties should differentiate difficulty and ease; strictly enforce coin prohibitions; broadly build up reserves; handle those who submit; reclaim fugitive soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for counsel, Wang Xin submitted ten proposals: guard against hasty changes in law; see that orders, once issued, are enforced; ease the burden on prefectures and commanderies to restore the people's strength; restore military discipline to await the right moment; let commanderies set priorities by urgency; let counties sort tasks by difficulty; enforce the ban on private coinage; build up stores of grain; settle those who surrender; and reclaim deserters.

sentences.zh: 起知湖州，信未涉州縣，據桉剖析，敏如流泉。

translations.literal: Recalled to serve as prefect of Huzhou—Wang Xin had not previously been involved in prefecture and county governance, yet sitting at his desk he analyzed cases with fluency like flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as prefect of Huzhou, Wang Xin had never held a local post; yet at his desk he dissected cases with the ease of running water.

sentences.zh: 擢集英殿修撰、知紹興府、浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler at the Hall for Cultivating Talent, made prefect of Shaoxing, and Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler at the Hall for Cultivating Talent, appointed prefect of Shaoxing, and made Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 奏免逋官錢十四萬、絹七萬匹、綿十萬五千兩、米二千萬斛。

translations.literal: He memorialized remission of fourteen myriad strings of overdue official money, seventy thousand bolts of silk, one hundred five thousand ounces of cotton, and twenty million hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for the remission of 140,000 strings of overdue official payments, 70,000 bolts of silk, 105,000 ounces of cotton, and 20 million hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 山陰境有𤠉�湖，四環皆田，歲苦潦，信創啟斗門，導停瀦注之海，築十一壩，化滙浸為上腴。

translations.literal: In the Shanyin region there was a lake [name corrupt in source]; encircled on four sides by fields, it suffered flooding every year. Wang Xin opened sluice gates, channeled the stagnant water to the sea, built eleven dams, and turned pooled inundation into rich soil.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shanyin region there was a lake surrounded on all sides by farmland that flooded every year. Wang Xin opened sluice gates, drained the stagnant water to the sea, built eleven dams, and turned marsh into fertile fields.

sentences.zh: 民繪象以祠，更其名曰「王公湖」。

translations.literal: The people painted his image for worship and changed the lake's name to "Lord Wang Lake."
translations.idiomatic: The people painted his portrait for veneration and renamed the lake Lord Wang Lake.

sentences.zh: 築漁浦隄，禁民不舉子，買學田，立義塚，眾職修理。

translations.literal: He built the Yubu embankment, forbade infanticide, purchased school lands, established public burial grounds, and attended to many such duties.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Yubu dike, forbade the abandonment of infants, bought land for schools, established charity graves, and carried out a host of such reforms.

sentences.zh: 加煥章閣待制，徙知鄂州，改池州。

translations.literal: Granted the title of Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Glorious Treasures, he was transferred to prefect of Ezhou, then changed to Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Made Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Glorious Treasures, he was transferred to Ezhou and then to Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，信扶其父喪歸自金陵，草屨徒行，雖疾風甚雨，弗避也，由是得寒濕疾。

translations.literal: Initially, when Wang Xin returned bearing his father's coffin from Jinling, he wore straw sandals and walked on foot; though fierce wind and heavy rain, he did not avoid them, and thereby contracted a cold-damp illness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, escorting his father's coffin home from Jinling, he wore straw sandals and went on foot through driving wind and rain without turning aside, and from that contracted a cold-damp disorder.

sentences.zh: 及聞孝宗遺詔，悲傷過甚，疾復作，至是寖劇，上章請老，以通議大夫致仕。

translations.literal: When he heard Emperor Xiaozong's death testament, his grief was excessive; his illness recurred, and by this time gradually worsened. He submitted a memorial requesting retirement and was granted retirement as Grand Master for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Emperor Xiaozong's final edict, his grief was overwhelming; his old illness returned and now grew steadily worse. He memorialized to retire and was granted retirement with the rank of Grand Master for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 有星隕於其居，光如炬，不及地數尺而散。

translations.literal: A star fell at his residence, its light like a torch, dispersing several feet before reaching the ground.
translations.idiomatic: A meteor fell at his home, blazing like a torch and vanishing a few feet above the ground.

sentences.zh: 數日，信卒，遺訓其子以忠孝公廉。

translations.literal: Several days later, Wang Xin died, leaving instructions to his son on loyalty, filial piety, public-mindedness, and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Wang Xin died, leaving his son a final charge to be loyal, filial, upright, and clean-handed.

sentences.zh: 所著有《是齋集》行世。

translations.literal: His collected works, Master of This Studio, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, Master of This Studio, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 汪大猷

translations.literal: Wang Dayou
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou

sentences.zh: 汪大猷，字仲嘉，慶元府鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Dayou, styled Zhongjia, was a native of Yin County in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou, courtesy name Zhongjia, was a native of Yin County in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興七年，以父恩補官，授衢州江山縣尉，曉暢吏事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shaoxing, through his father's grace he received office and was appointed magistrate of Jiangshan County in Quzhou; he was well versed in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Shaoxing he entered service through his father's privilege and was appointed magistrate of Jiangshan County in Quzhou, where he proved thoroughly capable in administrative matters.

sentences.zh: 登十五年進士第，授婺州金華縣丞，爭財者諭以長幼之禮，悅服而退。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Jinhua County in Wuzhou; those disputing over property he instructed in the rites of senior and junior, and they withdrew satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he passed the jinshi examination and was made assistant magistrate of Jinhua County in Wuzhou. When litigants quarreled over property, he explained the rites governing elder and younger kin, and they withdrew satisfied.

sentences.zh: 李椿年行經界法，約束嚴甚，檄大猷覆視龍遊縣，大猷請不實者得自陳，毋遽加罪。

translations.literal: Li Chunnian implemented the field-boundary law with very strict constraints; he dispatched Wang Dayou to re-inspect Longyou County. Wang Dayou requested that those whose reports were inaccurate be allowed to explain themselves and that punishment not be hastily applied.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chunnian enforced the land-survey law with harsh rigor, he sent Wang Dayou to re-inspect Longyou County. Wang Dayou asked that anyone found in error be allowed to plead his case and that penalties not be imposed in haste.

sentences.zh: 改建德，遷知崑山縣。

translations.literal: Reassigned to Jiande, he was then transferred to serve as magistrate of Kunshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jiande, he was next appointed magistrate of Kunshan County.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，免喪，差總領淮西、江東錢糧幹官，改幹辦行在諸司糧料院。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his father, he was assigned as administrative officer for grain and funds under the Huai West and Jiang East chief command, then changed to administrator of the provisional capital's grain ration office.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his father, he was assigned as grain-and-funds administrator for Huai West and Jiang East, then moved to the grain ration office of the mobile capital.

sentences.zh: 參知政事錢端禮宣諭淮東，辟幹辦公事，充參議官，遷大宗丞兼吏部郎官，又兼戶部右曹。

translations.literal: When Vice Grand Councillor Qian Duanli went to Huai East on an imperial mission, Wang Dayou was recruited as administrative secretary, served as advisory officer, transferred to Vice Director of the Great Ancestral Temple concurrently as Ministry of Personnel official, and also concurrently held the Right Section of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Grand Councillor Qian Duanli went east on an imperial mission to Huai, Wang Dayou joined his staff as administrative secretary and advisory officer, then rose to Vice Director of the Great Ancestral Temple with a concurrent post in the Ministry of Personnel, and later also served in the Right Section of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「總覈名實，責任臣下。

translations.literal: In audience he said: "Synthesize names and realities, and hold ministers responsible."
translations.idiomatic: Addressing the throne, he said: "Match names to realities and hold your ministers accountable."

sentences.zh: 因才而任，毋違所長，量能授官，毋拘流品。

translations.literal: "Assign according to talent without violating what each excels at; confer office according to capacity without being bound by bureaucratic rank."
translations.idiomatic: "Appoint men for what they can do, not against their strengths; grant office by measure of ability, not by fixed pedigree."

sentences.zh: 」孝宗顧謂左右曰：「疏通詳雅而善議論，有用之才也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong turned to those beside him and said: "Clear, thorough, refined and elegant, and skilled in discourse—a useful talent."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong turned to his attendants and said, "Clear, polished, and eloquent—a man of real use."

sentences.zh: 」除禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 丞相洪适薦兼吏部侍郎，仍遷主管左選。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Hong Shi recommended him to concurrently serve as Vice Minister of Personnel, and he was further transferred to supervise the Left Selection.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Hong Shi recommended him for concurrent service as Vice Minister of Personnel, and he was further placed in charge of the Left Selection.

sentences.zh: 莊文太子初建東宮，兼太子左諭德、侍講，兩日一講《孟子》，多寓規戒。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Zhuangwen first established the Eastern Palace, Wang Dayou concurrently served as Left Mentor and Lecturer to the Crown Prince, lecturing on the Mencius every two days, often embedding admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Zhuangwen first set up the Eastern Palace, Wang Dayou served concurrently as Left Mentor and Lecturer to the Crown Prince, expounding the Mencius every other day and weaving admonition into his teaching.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗出龍大淵禁中所進侍燕樂章，諭宮僚同賦，大猷曰：「鄭、衛之音，近習為倡，非講讀官所當預。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince once produced banquet entertainment lyrics that Long Dayuan had submitted from the inner palace and instructed the palace staff to compose matching verses. Wang Dayou said: "The music of Zheng and Wei is led by court favorites; it is not something lecturing officials ought to join in."
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince once circulated banquet lyrics that Long Dayuan had sent in from the inner palace and asked the palace staff to compose matching pieces. Wang Dayou said, "This is the licentious music of Zheng and Wei, with favorites at court setting the tone—it is no business of those who lecture and read to the heir."

sentences.zh: 」白於太子而止。

translations.literal: He reported this to the Crown Prince, and the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this to the Crown Prince, and the practice was halted.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書少監，修《五朝會要》。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and compiled the Collected Essentials of Five Reigns.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and worked on the Collected Essentials of Five Reigns.

sentences.zh: 金人來賀，假吏部尚書為接伴使。

translations.literal: When the Jin sent envoys to offer congratulations, he was temporarily appointed Minister of Personnel to serve as reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurchen envoys came to offer congratulations, he was temporarily appointed Minister of Personnel to serve as their reception commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋兼權刑部侍郎，又兼崇政殿說書，又兼給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently as Acting Vice Minister of Justice, then concurrently as Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, and again concurrently as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also held concurrent posts as Acting Vice Minister of Justice, Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, and Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 孝宗清燕，每訪政事，嘗曰：「朕每厭宦官女子之言，思與卿等款語，欲知朝政闕失，民情利病，苟有所聞，可極論之。

translations.literal: At Emperor Xiaozong's informal audiences he regularly inquired about governance and once said: "I tire of talk from eunuchs and palace women and wish to speak frankly with you. I want to learn of failures in court governance and what helps or harms the people. If you have heard anything, speak without reserve."
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Xiaozong's informal audiences he often discussed affairs of state and once said, "I am weary of hearing eunuchs and palace women, and I want to speak openly with you. I wish to know where court governance falls short and where the people's interests are helped or harmed. If you have heard anything, do not hold back—say all you know."

sentences.zh: 」大猷遂陳耆長雇直隸總經制司，並緣法意使里正兼催科之役，厲民為甚。

translations.literal: Wang Dayou then spoke of elders hiring salaried men attached to the General Commandery, and of village heads also burdened with tax collection under the law's intent—a grievous imposition on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou then raised the practice of village elders hiring salaried agents under the General Commandery, and the way the law was being read to make village heads perform tax collection as well—an onerous burden on the people indeed.

sentences.zh: 又論：「亭戶未嘗煮鹽，居近場監，貸錢射利，隱寄田產，害及編氓，宜取一等以上充役。

translations.literal: He argued further: "Registered salt households that have never boiled salt live near the salt offices, lend money for profit, and conceal land holdings elsewhere, harming registered taxpayers. Only households of the first rank and above should be conscripted for such duties."
translations.idiomatic: He argued further: "Many registered salt households have never actually boiled salt. They live near the salt offices, lend money for profit, and hide their land elsewhere, while the harm falls on ordinary registered taxpayers. Only households of the first rank and above should be pressed into such service."

sentences.zh: 」又論：「賜田勳戚，豪奪相先，陵轢州縣，惟當賜金，使自求之。

translations.literal: He argued further: "Granting land to meritorious kin leads them to seize it from one another and ride roughshod over prefectures and counties. They should receive gold instead and acquire land on their own."
translations.idiomatic: He argued further: "When land is granted to meritorious kin, they vie to seize it by force and bully prefectures and counties. They should be given gold instead and left to obtain land for themselves."

sentences.zh: 」又論：「沒入貲產，止可行於強盜、贓吏，至於倉庫綱運之負陷者，惟當即其業收租以償，既足則給還，使復故業。

translations.literal: He argued further: "Confiscation of property should apply only to armed robbers and corrupt officials. As for those who default on warehouse transport convoys, rent should be collected from their holdings to make restitution; once the debt is paid, their property should be returned so they may resume their former livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: He argued further: "Confiscation of property should be limited to armed robbers and corrupt officials. As for those who fall into debt on warehouse transport convoys, the state should collect rent from their holdings to make repayment; once the debt is satisfied, the property should be returned and they should be allowed to resume their former livelihood."

sentences.zh: 」轉對，言榷酒之害，及居官者不得鑄銅為器。

translations.literal: In rotating audience he spoke of the harm of the liquor monopoly and that officials must not cast copper into vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In a rotating palace audience he spoke of the evils of the liquor monopoly and of the prohibition on officials casting copper into vessels.

sentences.zh: 上嘉獎曰：「卿前後所言，皆今日可行之事。」

translations.literal: The Emperor praised him, saying: "What you have said throughout is all practicable today."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised him, saying, "Everything you have said, earlier and now, can be put into practice today."

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎，升侍講，言：「有司率用新制，棄舊法，輕重舛牾，無所遵承，使舞文之吏時出，以售其姦，請明詔編纂。

translations.literal: As Acting Vice Minister of Justice he was promoted to Lecturer-in-Attendance and said: "Offices habitually apply new regulations and discard old law; penalties clash and there is nothing to follow, allowing scriveners to appear at will and sell their deceit. I ask for an explicit edict to compile and codify the law."
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Acting Vice Minister of Justice, he was promoted to Lecturer-in-Attendance and said, "Offices routinely follow new rules and discard old statutes, so that penalties contradict one another and no one knows what to obey—giving manipulators of the written law room to appear and sell their tricks. I ask that an explicit edict order a compilation."

sentences.zh: 」書成上進，上大悅。

translations.literal: When the work was completed and submitted, the Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished and submitted, the Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 尚書周執羔、韓元吉、樞密劉珙以強盜率不處死，無所懲艾，右司林栗謂：「太祖朝強盜贓滿三貫死，無首從，不問殺傷。

translations.literal: Ministers Zhou Zhigao and Han Yuanji and Secretariat-Chancellery Chief Liu Gong held that robbers were rarely executed and there was no deterrent. Right Secretariat Official Lin Li said: "Under Taizu, robbery with loot worth three strings of cash was capital, regardless of leader or follower and without regard to killing or wounding."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Zhigao, Minister Han Yuanji, and Secretariat-Chancellery Chief Liu Gong argued that robbers were rarely put to death and that there was no real deterrent. Right Secretariat Official Lin Li said, "Under Taizu, robbery with loot worth three strings of cash was a capital offense, with no distinction between ringleader and follower and no inquiry into whether anyone had been killed or wounded."

sentences.zh: 景祐增五貫，固從寬。

translations.literal: Jingyou increased it to five strings—naturally lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingyou the threshold was raised to five strings—a deliberate easing.

sentences.zh: 今設六項法，非手刃人，例奏裁黥配，何所懲艾？

translations.literal: Now the six-item law is established; unless one kills with one's own hand, cases are routinely reported for imperial decision with tattooing and exile—what deterrent is there?
translations.idiomatic: Now the six-item law is in place: unless a robber kills with his own hand, cases are routinely sent up for imperial review and punished with tattooing and exile—where is the deterrent in that?

sentences.zh: 請從舊法，贓滿三貫者斬。

translations.literal: I ask that the old law be followed: those with loot of three strings or more should be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the old law be restored: anyone whose loot reaches three strings of cash should be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 」大猷曰：「此吾職也。

translations.literal: Wang Dayou said: "This is my duty."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou said, "This falls within my duty."

sentences.zh: 」遂具奏曰：「強盜烏可恕，用舊法而痛懲之，固可也。

translations.literal: He then submitted a detailed memorial, saying: "Robbers cannot be forgiven; applying the old law to punish them severely is certainly possible."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a full memorial, saying, "Robbers are not to be indulged, and it would certainly be possible to apply the old law and punish them harshly."

sentences.zh: 天聖以來，益用中典，寖失禁姦之意。

translations.literal: Since Tiansheng the middle standard has been used increasingly, gradually losing the intent to deter crime.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Tiansheng era, however, the middle standard of punishment has been used more and more, until the purpose of restraining crime has slowly been lost.

sentences.zh: 今所議六項法，犯者以法行之，非此而但取財，惟再犯者死，可謂寬嚴適中。

translations.literal: The six-item law now under discussion applies the law to those who qualify; those who merely take property without meeting those criteria die only on a second offense—this can be called balanced in severity and lenience.
translations.idiomatic: The six-item law now under discussion applies where the statute applies; where a robber merely takes property and does not fall under those categories, only a repeat offender is put to death. That can be called a balance of severity and lenience.

sentences.zh: 若皆置之死地，未必能禁其為盜，盜知必死，將甘心於事主矣，望稍開其生路。

translations.literal: If all were put to death, that would not necessarily stop robbery; knowing they must die, robbers would resign themselves to killing their victims. I hope a little room for life may be left open.
translations.idiomatic: If every robber were sent to death, that would not necessarily stop robbery. Once robbers know they must die, they will resign themselves to killing their victims as well. I hope Your Majesty will leave them some small path back to life.

sentences.zh: 」乃奏用六項法則死者十七人，用見行法則十四人，舊法百七十人俱死。

translations.literal: He reported that under the six-item law seventeen would die, under the law currently in force fourteen, and under the old law all one hundred seventy would die.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that under the six-item law seventeen would die, under the law then in force fourteen, and under the old law all one hundred seventy would die.

sentences.zh: 遂從大猷議。

translations.literal: The court adopted Wang Dayou's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court followed Wang Dayou's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 借吏部尚書為賀金國正旦使，至盱眙，得印榜云：「強盜止用舊法，罷六項法。

translations.literal: Temporarily holding the post of Minister of Personnel, he served as envoy to congratulate the Jin on New Year's Day. At Xuyi he obtained a printed placard saying: "For robbery only the old law is to be used; the six-item law is abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Serving temporarily as Minister of Personnel, he went as envoy to congratulate the Jin court on New Year's Day. At Xuyi he came upon a printed placard that read, "For robbery only the old law is to be used; the six-item law is abolished."

sentences.zh: 」還朝自劾求去，上聞之，復行六項法。

translations.literal: On returning to court he impeached himself and asked to leave office. When the Emperor heard of it, the six-item law was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he submitted a self-accusation and asked to be relieved of office. When the Emperor learned of the matter, the six-item law was put back into effect.

sentences.zh: 改權吏部侍郎兼權尚書。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent Acting Ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty as Acting Minister.

sentences.zh: 夜傳旨學士院，出唐沈既濟論選舉事，曰：「今日有此弊，可行與否，詰旦當面對。

translations.literal: At night an edict was sent to the Hanlin Academy, producing Tang Shen Jiji's essay on examination selection, saying: "Today we have this same abuse—can it be implemented or not? Tomorrow at dawn you will face me in audience."
translations.idiomatic: That night an edict was sent to the Hanlin Academy, along with the Tang writer Shen Jiji's essay on the selection examinations, saying, "This same abuse exists today—can his proposal be put into practice or not? Tomorrow at dawn you will answer me in person."

sentences.zh: 」即奏：「事與今異，弊雖似之，言則難行。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized: "The circumstances differ from today's; though the abuse resembles it, his proposal would be hard to put into practice."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately memorialized, "The circumstances are not the same as in his day. Though the abuse looks similar, what he proposes would be hard to carry out now."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言甚明。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your words are very clear."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Your explanation is very clear."

sentences.zh: 」既郊，差充鹵簿使，以言去，授敷文閣待制、提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: After the suburban sacrifice he was assigned as master of ceremonies for the imperial guard of honor; because of his frank speech he left office and was given the nominal posts of Attendant of the Fawen Pavilion and Director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he was assigned as commissioner of the imperial guard of honor, but because of his outspoken remonstrance he left office and was given the nominal posts of Attendant of the Fawen Pavilion and Director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 起知泉州。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 毗舍邪嘗掠海濱居民，歲遣戍防之，勞費不貲。

translations.literal: Pisheye had raided coastal residents; each year garrison troops were sent to guard against them, at immense labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Pisheye raiders had preyed on coastal inhabitants, and every year garrison troops were sent to guard against them, at enormous labor and cost.

sentences.zh: 大猷作屋二百區，遣將留屯。

translations.literal: Wang Dayou built two hundred quarters and dispatched generals to remain garrisoned there.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou built two hundred dwellings and sent officers to remain stationed there.

sentences.zh: 久之，戍兵以真臘大買為毗舍邪犯境，大猷曰：「毗舍邪面目黑如漆，語言不通，此豈毗舍邪耶？

translations.literal: After some time the garrison reported Khmer merchants as Pisheye raiding the border. Wang Dayou said: "Pisheye have faces black as lacquer and speak an unintelligible tongue—how could these men be Pisheye?"
translations.idiomatic: After some time the garrison reported that Khmer merchants were Pisheye raiders violating the border. Wang Dayou said, "Pisheye have faces black as lacquer and speak a language we cannot understand—how could these men be Pisheye?"

sentences.zh: 」遂遣之。

translations.literal: He had them sent away.
translations.idiomatic: He had them released and sent on their way.

sentences.zh: 故事蕃商與人爭鬥，非傷折罪，皆以牛贖，大猷曰：「安有中國用島夷俗者，苟在吾境，當用吾法。

translations.literal: By precedent, when foreign merchants fought and no broken bones resulted, all redeemed guilt with cattle. Wang Dayou said: "How can the Middle Kingdom follow island barbarian custom? If they are within our territory, our law should apply."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when foreign merchants quarreled and no bones were broken, all parties redeemed the offense with cattle. Wang Dayou said, "How can the Middle Kingdom adopt the customs of island barbarians? So long as they are within our territory, our law should govern them."

sentences.zh: 」三佛齊請鑄銅瓦三萬，詔泉、廣二州守臣督造付之。

translations.literal: Srivijaya requested thirty thousand cast copper tiles; an edict ordered the prefects of Quan and Guang to supervise production and deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: Srivijaya requested thirty thousand cast copper tiles, and an edict ordered the prefects of Quan and Guang to supervise their manufacture and deliver them.

sentences.zh: 大猷奏：「法，銅不下海。

translations.literal: Wang Dayou memorialized: "By law, copper must not go to sea."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou memorialized, "By law, copper is not to be sent overseas."

sentences.zh: 中國方禁銷銅，奈何為其所役？

translations.literal: The Middle Kingdom is presently forbidding the melting of copper—how can we be put to work for them?
translations.idiomatic: The empire is now forbidding the melting down of copper—how can we be made to labor on their behalf?

sentences.zh: 」卒不與。

translations.literal: In the end he did not supply them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused to provide them.

sentences.zh: 進敷文閣直學士，留知泉州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Direct Academician of the Fawen Pavilion and remained prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Academician of the Fawen Pavilion and continued as prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，提舉太平興國宮，改知隆興府、江西安撫使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was made Director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace and transferred to serve as prefect of Longxing Prefecture and Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made Director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace and transferred to serve as prefect of Longxing and Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以大暑討永新禾山洞寇，不利，自劾，降龍圖閣待制，落職，南康軍居住，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: In the height of summer he campaigned against bandits in the Hemiao Mountain caves of Yongxin; the expedition went badly. He impeached himself, was demoted to Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion, stripped of rank, ordered to reside at Nankang Prefecture, and given charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the height of summer he led a campaign against bandits in the Hemiao Mountain caves of Yongxin, but the operation went badly. He submitted a self-accusation, was demoted to Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion, stripped of office, ordered to reside at Nankang, and given charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 復龍圖閣待制，提舉上清太平宮。

translations.literal: He was restored to Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion and made Director of the Shangqing Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion and made Director of the Shangqing Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 復敷文閣待制，升學士。

translations.literal: He was again made Attendant of the Fawen Pavilion and promoted to Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Attendant of the Fawen Pavilion and promoted to Academician.

sentences.zh: 沒，贈二官。

translations.literal: When he died, two ranks of posthumous office were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously granted two ranks of office.

sentences.zh: 大猷與丞相史浩同里，又同年進士，未嘗附麗以干進，浩深歎美之。

translations.literal: Wang Dayou was from the same district as Grand Councillor Shi Hao and had passed the jinshi in the same year, yet never attached himself to Hao to advance his career—Hao admired this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou was a townsman of Grand Councillor Shi Hao and had passed the jinshi examination in the same year, yet he never clung to Hao to advance himself—a fact Hao admired deeply.

sentences.zh: 好周施，敘宗族外族為《興仁錄》，率鄉人為義莊二十餘畝以爲倡，眾皆欣勸。

translations.literal: He loved generous giving. He compiled a Record of Fostering Benevolence for his clan and allied families, and led his countrymen in establishing a charity estate of more than twenty mu as an example; all gladly followed his encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of generous charity. He compiled a Record of Fostering Benevolence for his clan and related families, and led his fellow townsmen in founding a charity estate of more than twenty mu as an example; everyone gladly took up his call.

sentences.zh: 所著有《適齋存藁》、《備忘》、《訓鑒》等書。

translations.literal: His written works include Collected Drafts of the Appropriate Studio, Memoranda, Instruction and Mirror, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: His publications included Collected Drafts of the Appropriate Studio, Memoranda, Instruction and Mirror, and other works.

sentences.zh: 袁燮，字和叔，慶元府鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Yuan Xie, style name Heshu, was a native of Yin County in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie, courtesy name Heshu, came from Yin County in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 生而端粹專靜，乳媼置盤水其前，玩視終日，夜臥常醒然。

translations.literal: From birth he was upright, pure, focused, and quiet; when his nursemaid placed a basin of water before him, he would gaze at it all day; even at night he slept lightly and remained alert.
translations.idiomatic: From infancy he was upright, pure, and inwardly still. When his nurse set a basin of water before him, he would stare at it all day long; at night he slept lightly, always wakeful rather than sunk in oblivion.

sentences.zh: 少長，讀東都《黨錮傳》，慨然以名節自期。

translations.literal: As he grew, he read the Biographies of the Partisan Proscriptions from the Eastern Capital and, moved, set his heart on reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When he was older, he read the Biographies of the Partisan Proscriptions from the Eastern Capital and resolved, with deep feeling, to measure his life by honor and principle.

sentences.zh: 入太學，登進士第，調江陰尉。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University, passed the jinshi examination, and was assigned as defense commandant of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University, took his jinshi degree, and was posted as defense commandant of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 浙西大饑，常平使羅點屬任振恤。

translations.literal: When western Zhe suffered a great famine, Luo Dian, Ever-Normal Granary commissioner, entrusted Xie with relief work.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck western Zhe, Luo Dian, the Ever-Normal Granary commissioner, put Xie in charge of relief.

sentences.zh: 燮命每保畫一圖，田疇、山水、道路悉載之，而以居民分布其間，凡名數、治業悉書之。

translations.literal: Xie ordered that every bao draw one map, recording fields, rivers and mountains, and roads in full, with residents placed among them, writing down all names and numbers and every occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Xie ordered each bao to draw a map recording every field, waterway, hill, and road, with households marked among them and every name, headcount, and livelihood noted in full.

sentences.zh: 合保為都，合都為鄉，合鄉為縣，征發、爭訟、追胥，披圖可立決，以此為荒政首。

translations.literal: Bao were combined into du, du into xiang, and xiang into counties; for conscription, lawsuits, and tax collection, one could unfold the maps and decide at once—he made this the foremost method of famine administration.
translations.idiomatic: Bao were grouped into du, du into townships, townships into counties; for levies, litigation, and tax collection, he could unroll a map and settle the matter on the spot. He ranked this first among famine-relief methods.

sentences.zh: 除沿海制屬。

translations.literal: He was appointed staff member on the coastal defense commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a staff officer on the coastal defense commission.

sentences.zh: 連丁家艱，寧宗即位，以太學正召。

translations.literal: He observed mourning in succession for both parents; when Emperor Ningzong took the throne, he was summoned as Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning both parents in succession, he was recalled as Director of the Imperial University when Ningzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 時朱熹諸儒相次去國，丞相趙汝愚罷，燮亦以論去，自是黨禁興矣。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Xi and other scholars left court in succession; Grand Councillor Zhao Ruyu was dismissed; Xie likewise left because of a memorial—and from this the partisan proscription began.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi and other scholars were leaving court one after another; Grand Councillor Zhao Ruyu had been dismissed; Xie, too, was driven out after memorializing the throne—and the factional proscription began.

sentences.zh: 久之，為浙東帥幕、福建常平屬、沿海參議。

translations.literal: After some time he served as staff officer to the Eastern Zhe military commissioner, staff member of the Fujian Ever-Normal Granary, and coastal defense advisory officer.
translations.idiomatic: In time he served on the staff of the Eastern Zhe military commissioner, as an officer of the Fujian Ever-Normal Granary, and as a coastal defense adviser.

sentences.zh: 嘉定初，召主宗正簿、樞密院編修官，權考功郎官、太常丞、知江州，改提舉江西常平、權知隆興。

translations.literal: In the early Jiading reign he was summoned to serve as Registrar in the Directorate of the Imperial Clan and Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, acting official in the Ministry of Personnel's Department of Merit and Demerit, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Prefect of Jiangzhou; he was then changed to Intendant of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary and acting Prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiading reign he was recalled as registrar of the Imperial Clan directorate and compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, then served concurrently as acting merit-and-demerit officer in the Ministry of Personnel, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and prefect of Jiangzhou, before becoming intendant of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granary with acting authority over Longxing.

sentences.zh: 召為都官郎官，遷司封。

translations.literal: He was summoned as official of the Department of Punishments in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to the Department of Enfeoffment in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Called back as an official in the Ministry of Justice's Department of Punishments, he was promoted to the Enfeoffment office in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 因對，言：「陛下即位之初，委任賢相，正士鱗集，而竊威權者從旁睨之。

translations.literal: At an audience he said: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's reign, you entrusted a worthy chief minister; upright men gathered like fish scales—yet those who stole authority watched from the side.
translations.idiomatic: Addressing the throne, he said, "When Your Majesty first took the throne, you entrusted a worthy chief minister and upright men thronged the court—while men who coveted power watched from the sidelines.

sentences.zh: 彭龜年逆知其必亂天下，顯言其姦，龜年以罪去，而權臣遂根據，幾危社稷。

translations.literal: Peng Guinian foresaw that such men would surely throw the realm into chaos and openly exposed their wickedness; Peng was driven out on criminal charges, and the powerful minister then entrenched himself, nearly endangering the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Guinian saw in advance that they would wreck the realm and denounced their treachery openly. Peng was dismissed on fabricated charges, the power-holder dug in, and the state came close to ruin.

sentences.zh: 陛下追思龜年，蓋嘗臨朝太息曰：『斯人猶在，必大用之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, recalling Peng Guinian, once sighed at court and said: 'If this man were still alive, he would surely be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, looking back on Peng Guinian, once sighed at court and said, 'If that man were still alive, I would put him to great use.

sentences.zh: 』固已深知龜年之忠矣。

translations.literal: ' You already knew deeply that Peng was loyal.
translations.idiomatic: ' You already knew full well how loyal Peng was.

sentences.zh: 今正人端士不乏，願陛下常存此心，急聞剴切，崇獎樸直，一龜年雖沒，眾龜年繼進，天下何憂不治。

translations.literal: Today worthy and upright men are not lacking; I beg Your Majesty to keep this heart always, to heed earnest and cutting counsel urgently, to honor plain and straightforward men—and though one Peng Guinian has died, many Peng Guinians may follow; why should the realm fear it will not be well governed?
translations.idiomatic: Worthy, upright men are not scarce even now. If Your Majesty keeps this disposition, listens eagerly to forthright counsel, and rewards plainspoken integrity, then though one Peng Guinian is gone, others like him will come forward—and what governable realm could not be brought to order?

sentences.zh: 臣昨勸陛下勤於好問，而聖訓有曰：『問則明』。

translations.literal: Your subject yesterday urged Your Majesty to be diligent in asking questions, and the imperial instruction says: 'To ask is to be enlightened.'
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I urged Your Majesty to question more readily, and Your Majesty answered, 'He who asks will understand.'

sentences.zh: 臣退與朝士言之，莫不稱善。

translations.literal: When I withdrew and spoke of this to court colleagues, all praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When I left and told my colleagues at court, every one of them approved.

sentences.zh: 而側聽十旬，陛下之端拱淵默猶昔也，臣竊惑焉。

translations.literal: Yet listening from the side for ten ten-day periods, Your Majesty sits formally in profound silence as before; your subject is privately puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for a hundred days I have watched from the sidelines, and Your Majesty still sits in formal silence, deep and still as before. I confess I am troubled.

sentences.zh: 夫既知如是而明，則當知反是而暗。

translations.literal: If you know that the one brings enlightenment, you should know that the opposite brings darkness.
translations.idiomatic: If one knows that asking brings light, one should know that the opposite brings darkness.

sentences.zh: 明則輝光旁燭，無所不通；

translations.literal: In light, radiance shines to every side and nothing is blocked;
translations.idiomatic: In light, brilliance spreads in every direction and nothing stays closed;

sentences.zh: 暗則是非得失，懵然不辨矣。」

translations.literal: in darkness, right and wrong, gain and loss—all are confused beyond distinction."
translations.idiomatic: in darkness, right and wrong, gain and loss blur together beyond telling."

sentences.zh: 遷國子司業、秘書少監，進祭酒、秘書監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the National University and Vice Director of the Palace Library, then advanced to Chancellor of the National University and Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the National University and vice director of the Palace Library, then to chancellor of the National University and director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 延見諸生，必迪以反躬切己，忠信篤實，是為道本。

translations.literal: Whenever he received students, he always instructed them to turn inward and examine themselves earnestly, and to take loyalty, faithfulness, sincerity, and solidity as the root of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met students, he always pressed them to look inward and hold themselves to account, taking loyalty, trustworthiness, and solid integrity as the foundation of learning.

sentences.zh: 聞者悚然有得，士氣益振。

translations.literal: Those who heard him were startled into understanding; morale among the scholars rose.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners came away startled and enriched; the spirit of the student body revived.

sentences.zh: 兼崇政殿說書，除禮部侍郎兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Concurrently Lecturer at the Hall of Cultivating Governance; appointed Vice Minister of Rites and Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He also lectured at the Hall of Cultivating Governance and was appointed vice minister of rites with concurrent duties as lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 時史彌遠主和，燮爭益力，臺論劾燮，罷之，以寶文閣待制提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Miyuan advocated peace; Xie argued more fiercely; the censorate impeached Xie and he was dismissed, made Attendant Gentleman of the Hall of Treasured Literature with appointment as superintendent of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan then led the peace party, and Xie opposed him ever more forcefully. The censorate impeached Xie and removed him, assigning him attendant gentleman at the Hall of Treasured Literature and superintendent of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 起知溫州，進直學士，奉祠以卒。

translations.literal: Recalled to serve as prefect of Wenzhou, he was promoted to Hanlin academy scholar and died while holding a temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as prefect of Wenzhou and promoted to Hanlin academician, he died in a temple sinecure post.

sentences.zh: 燮初入太學，陸九齡為學錄，同里沈煥、楊簡、舒璘亦皆在學，以道義相切磨。

translations.literal: When Xie first entered the Imperial University, Lu Jiuling was Recorder; Shen Huan, Yang Jian, and Shu Lin of the same district were also in the school, and they honed one another through shared moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie first entered the Imperial University, Lu Jiuling was recorder; his fellow townsmen Shen Huan, Yang Jian, and Shu Lin were there as well, and they sharpened one another in the discipline of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 後見九齡之弟九淵，發明本心之指，乃師事焉。

translations.literal: Later he met Jiuling's younger brother Jiuyuan, who elucidated the doctrine of the original mind; he then took Jiuyuan as his master.
translations.idiomatic: Later he met Jiuling's younger brother Jiuyuan, who unfolded the teaching of the original mind, and became his disciple.

sentences.zh: 每言人心與天地一本，精思以得之，兢業以守之則與天地相似。

translations.literal: He often said that the human mind and Heaven-and-Earth share one root; obtain it through refined thought and preserve it through reverent diligence, and one will resemble Heaven-and-Earth.
translations.idiomatic: He would say that the human mind and Heaven-and-Earth are of one root: attain it through keen reflection, guard it through conscientious diligence, and one becomes akin to Heaven-and-Earth.

sentences.zh: 學者稱之曰「潔齋先生」。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Jiezhai.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honored him as Master Jiezhai.

sentences.zh: 後諡「正獻」。

translations.literal: Later he was given the posthumous title "Correct Contribution."
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the posthumous title Correct Contribution.

sentences.zh: 子：甫，自有傳。

translations.literal: Son: Fu, who has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 吳柔勝

translations.literal: Wu Rousheng
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rousheng

sentences.zh: 吳柔勝，字勝之，宣州人。

translations.literal: Wu Rousheng, style name Shengzhi, was a native of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rousheng, courtesy name Shengzhi, came from Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼聽其父講伊、洛書，已知有持敬之學，不妄言笑。

translations.literal: In youth, listening to his father expound the books of the Yiluo tradition, he already knew there was a learning of reverent attentiveness, and did not speak or laugh lightly.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, hearing his father explain the Cheng-Zhu texts, he already understood the discipline of reverent attentiveness and never jested or laughed lightly.

sentences.zh: 長遊郡泮，人皆憚其方嚴。

translations.literal: When grown, he studied at the prefectural school; all feared his rigor and solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he entered the prefectural academy, where everyone stood in awe of his stern rectitude.

sentences.zh: 登淳熙八年進士第，調都昌簿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chunxi he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as registrar of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the eighth year of the Chunxi reign and was posted as registrar of Duchang.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙汝愚知其賢，差嘉興府學教授，將置之館閣，會汝愚去，御史湯碩劾柔勝嘗救荒浙右，擅放田租，為汝愚收人心，且主朱熹之學，不可為師儒官，自是閑居十餘年。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Zhao Ruyu knew his worth and assigned him professor at the Jiaxing prefectural school, intending to place him in the palace archive; but when Zhao Ruyu fell, Supervising Censor Tang Shuo impeached Rousheng, saying that in relieving famine in western Zhe he had arbitrarily remitted field rent to win hearts for Zhao Ruyu and that, moreover, he upheld Zhu Xi's learning and was unfit for instructor posts—whereupon he lived in retirement for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Zhao Ruyu recognized his talent, made him professor at the Jiaxing prefectural school, and planned to move him into the Hanlin archive. Then Zhao Ruyu fell. Supervising Censor Tang Shuo impeached Rousheng for having remitted field rent on his own authority while relieving famine in western Zhe—an effort, Tang charged, to win popular favor for Zhao Ruyu—and for teaching Zhu Xi's doctrines, unfit for a post as master of scholars. Rousheng then lived quietly at home for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 嘉定初，主管刑、工部架閣文字，遷國子正。

translations.literal: In the early Jiading reign he was put in charge of archive documents for the Ministries of Justice and of Works and was promoted to Director of Students at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiading reign he managed archival records for the ministries of justice and works, then rose to director of students at the National University.

sentences.zh: 柔勝始以朱熹《四書》與諸生誦習，講義策問，皆以是為先。

translations.literal: Rousheng began having students recite Zhu Xi's Four Books; in lectures, policy questions, and examinations, he always put these first.
translations.idiomatic: Rousheng had students begin with recitation of Zhu Xi's Four Books and made them the first priority in lectures, essays, and examinations.

sentences.zh: 又於生徒中得潘時舉、呂喬年，白於長，擢為職事，使以文行表率，於是士知趨向，伊、洛之學，晦而復明。

translations.literal: Among his pupils he singled out Pan Shiju and Lu Qiaonian, reported them to the chief officer, and promoted them to student officers, making them models of learning and conduct—whereupon scholars knew which way to turn, and Yiluo learning, though darkened, brightened again.
translations.idiomatic: He identified Pan Shiju and Lu Qiaonian among his students, recommended them to the head of the school, and raised them to student officers to model learning and conduct. From then on students knew what to strive for, and the learning of Luoyang, once eclipsed, dawned again.

sentences.zh: 遷太學博士，又遷司農寺丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University and then to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue's agriculture section.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to erudite of the Imperial University, then to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's agriculture section.

sentences.zh: 出知隨州。

translations.literal: He left the capital to serve as prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 時再議和好，尤戒開邊隙，旁塞之民事與北界相涉，不問法輕重皆殺之。

translations.literal: At that time peace was again under discussion and every care was taken to avoid border incidents; when affairs of people along the frontier garrisons touched the northern border, regardless of whether the law was light or heavy, all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Peace talks were underway again, and officials were especially anxious not to provoke border clashes. Whenever a frontier resident's case touched Jin territory, the accused were put to death without regard to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 郡民梁臯有馬為北人所盜，追之急，北人以矢拒臯，臯與其徒亦發二矢。

translations.literal: A man of the prefecture, Liang Gao, had a horse stolen by northerners; in pressing the pursuit closely, the northerners repelled Gao with arrows, and Gao and his followers loosed two arrows in return.
translations.idiomatic: A prefectural subject named Liang Gao had his horse stolen by Jin subjects. He gave chase hotly; the northerners drove him off with arrows, and Gao and his companions shot back twice.

sentences.zh: 北界以為言，郡下七人於獄，柔勝至，立破械縱之，具始末報北界而已。

translations.literal: The northern border raised the matter; seven men of the prefecture were in prison. When Rousheng arrived, he immediately broke their shackles and released them, and simply reported the full course of events to the northern border authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin border lodged a complaint, and seven local men were thrown into jail. As soon as Rousheng took up his post, he had their fetters struck off and set them free, then sent the northern authorities a full account of what had happened—and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 收土豪孟宗政、扈再興隸帳下，後宗政、再興皆為名將。
