translations.literal: He took in the local strongmen Meng Zongzheng and Hu Zaixing under his command; later both Zongzheng and Zaixing became famous generals.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the local strongmen Meng Zongzheng and Hu Zaixing into his service; both later rose to become celebrated commanders.

sentences.zh: 築隨州及棗陽城，招四方亡命得千人，立軍曰「忠勇」，廩以總所闕額，營柵器械悉備。

translations.literal: He built fortifications at Suizhou and Zaoyang, recruited a thousand fugitives from all quarters, established an army called "Loyal Valor," supplied it from the shortfall in the general headquarters quota, and fully equipped camps, stockades, and arms.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Suizhou and Zaoyang, gathered a thousand desperate men from every direction, and raised a unit called the Loyal Valor Army, drawing its rations from the headquarters shortfall while equipping its camps, palisades, and weapons in full.

sentences.zh: 除京西提刑，領州如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Judicial Intendant of Jingxi while retaining his prefectural duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Judicial Intendant of Jingxi Circuit but continued to govern his prefecture as before.

sentences.zh: 改湖北運判兼知鄂州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Transport Commissioner of Hubei while also serving as prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Transport Commissioner of Hubei and given concurrent appointment as prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 甫至，值歲歉，即乞糴於湖南，大講荒政，十五州被災之民，全活者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Hardly had he arrived when the year was lean; he immediately requested grain purchases from Hunan and launched a major famine-relief program; among the people of fifteen disaster-stricken prefectures, those wholly saved were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely arrived when famine struck. He at once petitioned to buy grain from Hunan and mounted a sweeping relief campaign; across fifteen stricken prefectures, the lives he preserved were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 改知太平州，除直秘閣，主管毫州明道宮。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Taiping Prefecture, appointed Direct Attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion, and made Superintendent of the Mingdao Abbey in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as prefect of Taiping, appointed Direct Attendant of the Secretariat Pavilion, and put in charge of the Mingdao Abbey in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 改直華文閣，除工部郎中，力辭，除秘閣修撰，依舊宮觀以卒，諡「正肅」。

translations.literal: He was changed to Direct Attendant of the Huawen Pavilion and appointed Director in the Ministry of Works; he forcefully declined; he was then appointed Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion and died while still holding his Taoist abbey post; his posthumous title was "Zhengsu."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Direct Attendant of the Huawen Pavilion and offered the directorship of the Ministry of Works, he firmly refused; he was then made Compiler of the Secretariat Pavilion and died while still serving in his abbey sinecure, posthumously titled Upright and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 二子：淵、潛，俱登進士，各有傳。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Yuan and Qian; both passed the jinshi examination, and each has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons, Yuan and Qian, both took the jinshi degree; each has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 遊仲鴻

translations.literal: You Zhonghong
translations.idiomatic: You Zhonghong

sentences.zh: 遊仲鴻，字子正，果之南充人。

translations.literal: You Zhonghong, style name Zizheng, was a native of Nanchong in Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: You Zhonghong, courtesy name Zizheng, came from Nanchong in Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年進士第，初調犍為簿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunxi he passed the jinshi examination; his first assignment was as registrar of Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the second year of Chunxi and was first posted as registrar of Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 李昌圖總蜀賦，辟糴買官，奇其才，曰：「吾董餉積年，惟得一士。

translations.literal: Li Changtu oversaw Shu tax collection and recruited him as grain-purchase officer; marveling at his talent, he said: "In all my years supervising provisions, I have found only one true gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changtu, who managed Sichuan revenue, brought him on as grain-purchase officer. Struck by his ability, Li said, "In all the years I have overseen supplies, I have found only one man of real worth.

sentences.zh: 」昌圖召入，首薦之，擢四川制置司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: " Changtu summoned him to the capital, recommended him first among candidates, and promoted him to staff officer of the Sichuan Commissioner-in-Chief's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " Li summoned him to the capital, put his name at the head of the recommendations, and raised him to staff officer on the Sichuan Commissioner-in-Chief's staff.

sentences.zh: 制置使趙汝愚一見即知敬之。

translations.literal: Commissioner Zhao Ruyu, upon a single meeting, knew to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Zhao Ruyu recognized his worth at first sight and treated him with deference.

sentences.zh: 敘州董蠻犯犍為境，憲將合兵討之，仲鴻請行。

translations.literal: The Dong tribes of Xuzhou violated the border of Qianwei; the intendant was about to combine forces to punish them, and Zhonghong volunteered to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dong tribes of Xuzhou raided Qianwei, the circuit intendant prepared to muster troops for a punitive campaign; Zhonghong asked to go himself.

sentences.zh: 詰其釁端，以州負馬直也，乃使人諭蠻曰：「歸俘則還馬直，不然大兵至矣。

translations.literal: On examining the cause of the conflict, it was because the prefecture owed payment for horses; he sent someone to instruct the tribes, saying: "Return the captives and we will repay the horse price; otherwise great armies will come.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating how the trouble began, he found the prefecture owed them payment for horses. He sent an envoy to tell the tribes, "Return our prisoners and the horse money will be paid; refuse, and a large force will march on you.

sentences.zh: 」蠻聽命，仲鴻受其降而歸。

translations.literal: " The tribes obeyed; Zhonghong accepted their surrender and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " The tribes complied. Zhonghong accepted their submission and came home.

sentences.zh: 改秩，知中江縣，總領楊輔檄置幕下。

translations.literal: After a change in rank he became magistrate of Zhongjiang County; Overall Commander Yang Fu summoned him by dispatch to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted in rank, he was made magistrate of Zhongjiang; Overall Commander Yang Fu then called him to his secretariat by written order.

sentences.zh: 時關外營田凡萬四千頃，畝僅輸七升。

translations.literal: At the time garrison farms beyond the pass totaled fourteen thousand qing; each mu yielded only seven sheng in tax.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison farms outside the passes then covered fourteen thousand qing in all, yet each mu paid barely seven sheng in grain.

sentences.zh: 仲鴻建議，請以兵之當汰者授之田，存赤籍，遲以數年，汰者眾，耕者多，則橫斂一切之賦可次第以減。

translations.literal: Zhonghong proposed granting fields to soldiers slated for demobilization, retaining the original registries, and waiting several years; as demobilizations increased and cultivators multiplied, arbitrary levies and miscellaneous taxes could then be reduced in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghong urged that soldiers marked for demobilization be given land while keeping the original military rolls on file; after a few years, as more men were mustered out and more fields were tilled, the crushing surcharges and assorted exactions could be cut back step by step.

sentences.zh: 輔然之，大將吳挺沮而止。

translations.literal: Fu approved, but the great general Wu Ting obstructed it and the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fu agreed, but the senior commander Wu Ting blocked the proposal and it came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚移帥閩，舉仲鴻自代，制置使京鏜、轉運劉光祖亦交薦於朝。

translations.literal: When Zhao Ruyu moved to command Fujian, he recommended Zhonghong as his replacement; Commissioner Jing Tang and Transport Commissioner Liu Guangzu also jointly recommended him to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ruyu transferred to command Fujian, he nominated Zhonghong to succeed him; Commissioner Jing Tang and Transport Commissioner Liu Guangzu likewise recommended him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年，赴召，趙汝愚在樞密，謂仲鴻直諒多聞，訪以蜀中利病。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxi he answered the summons; Zhao Ruyu was at the Bureau of Military Affairs and, deeming Zhonghong straightforward, honest, and widely learned, consulted him on the benefits and harms of Shu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shaoxi he came to court on summons. Zhao Ruyu, then at the Bureau of Military Affairs, judged him upright, candid, and well informed, and questioned him closely on Sichuan's strengths and weaknesses.

sentences.zh: 汝愚欲親出經略西事，仲鴻曰：「宥密之地，斡旋者易，公獨不聞呂申公『經略西事當在朝廷』之語乎？

translations.literal: Ruyu wished to go out in person to manage western affairs; Zhonghong said: "At the Privy Council, maneuvering is easy—have you alone not heard Minister Lü's words that 'managing western affairs ought to be done at court'?
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu wanted to take the field himself to oversee the west. Zhonghong said, "In the Privy Council you can turn affairs with a word—surely you have not forgotten what Lord Lü said: 'Western strategy belongs at court'?

sentences.zh: 」汝愚悟而止。

translations.literal: " Ruyu understood and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruyu took the point and gave up the idea.

sentences.zh: 差幹辦諸司糧料院。

translations.literal: He was assigned as staff officer of the Provisionery for All Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as staff officer of the Provisionery for All Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 汝愚既拜右丞相，以仲鴻久遊其門，辟嫌不用。

translations.literal: Once Ruyu had been appointed Right Grand Councillor, because Zhonghong had long been associated with his faction, he avoided favoritism and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruyu became Right Grand Councillor, he declined to use Zhonghong, lest their long association be read as cronyism.

sentences.zh: 初，汝愚之定策也，知閤韓侂胄頗有勞，望節鉞，汝愚不與。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Ruyu settled the succession plan, Director of the Palace Gate Han Tuozhou had contributed considerably and hoped for a military commission; Ruyu did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyu had first engineered the succession, Palace Gate Director Han Tuozhou had done much of the work and expected a field command; Ruyu refused him.

sentences.zh: 侂胄方居中用事，恚甚。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was then wielding power from within the palace and was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was already the power behind the throne, and he burned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 汝愚迹已危，方益自嚴重，選人求見者例不許。

translations.literal: Ruyu's position was already perilous; he became all the more stern and reserved, and routinely refused office-seekers who wished audience.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyu's footing was already precarious. He grew only more guarded and austere, turning away petitioners as a rule.

sentences.zh: 仲鴻勸以降意容接，覬遏異論，而汝愚以淮東、西總賦積弊，奏遣仲鴻覈實，仲鴻曰：「丞相之勢已孤，不憂此而顧憂彼耶？

translations.literal: Zhonghong urged him to lower his manner and receive people openly, hoping to check divergent opinion; but Ruyu cited chronic abuses in overall tax collection for Huai-East and Huai-West and memorialized to send Zhonghong to verify them; Zhonghong said: "The Grand Councillor's position is already isolated—why worry about that and not this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghong urged him to soften his bearing and meet callers openly, hoping to stifle hostile talk. Instead Ruyu cited entrenched abuses in overall tax collection on the Huai rivers and sent Zhonghong to investigate. Zhonghong said, "Your power is already standing alone—is this really the moment to worry about that rather than this?

sentences.zh: 」改監登聞鼓院以行。

translations.literal: " He was changed to supervisor of the Petition Drum Court and sent on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: " He was reassigned to supervise the Petition Drum Court and sent away on the assignment.

sentences.zh: 會侍講朱熹以論事去國，仲鴻聞之，即上疏曰：「陛下宅憂之時，御批數出，不由中書。

translations.literal: When Lecturer-in-Waiting Zhu Xi left office over policy disputes, Zhonghong heard and immediately submitted a memorial, saying: "While Your Majesty is in mourning, imperial rescripts issue repeatedly without passing through the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Lecturer-in-Waiting Zhu Xi was driven from court for his remonstrance, Zhonghong at once memorialized: "In this period of imperial mourning, rescripts pour forth without the Secretariat's review.

sentences.zh: 前日宰相留正之去，去之不以禮；

translations.literal: The other day Chancellor Liu Zheng left—not dismissed with proper rites;
translations.idiomatic: First Chancellor Liu Zheng was removed—without the courtesy owed a chief minister;

sentences.zh: 諫官黃度之去，去之不以正；

translations.literal: Remonstrance Officer Huang Du left—not dismissed with propriety;
translations.idiomatic: then Remonstrance Officer Huang Du was removed—without justice;

sentences.zh: 近臣朱熹之去，復去之不以道。

translations.literal: the close minister Zhu Xi has left again—not dismissed by proper means.
translations.idiomatic: and now the intimate adviser Zhu Xi has been removed again—without right principle.

sentences.zh: 自古未有舍宰相、諫官、講官而能自為聰明者也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity there has never been one who could be wise on his own while discarding the Chancellor, remonstrance officers, and lecture officials.
translations.idiomatic: Never in history has any ruler been truly wise while casting aside his chancellor, his remonstrators, and his lecturers.

sentences.zh: 願亟還熹，毋使小人得志，以養成禍亂。」

translations.literal: I beg that Xi be quickly restored, lest petty men prevail and catastrophe be nurtured."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to recall Xi at once, lest small men triumph and disaster take root."

sentences.zh: 監察御史胡紘希侂胄意，誣汝愚久蓄邪心，嘗語人以乘龍授鼎之夢，又謂朝士中有推其宗派，以為裔出楚王元佐，正統所在者，指仲鴻也。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Hu Gong, wishing to please Tuozhou, slandered Ruyu for long harboring treacherous intent, saying he had told people of a dream of riding a dragon and receiving the cauldron, and that among court officials some traced his lineage, holding that one descended from Prince Yuanzuo of Chu represented legitimate succession—the one pointed to was Zhonghong.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Hu Gong, eager to curry favor with Tuozhou, accused Ruyu of long-nurtured treason, claiming he had spoken to others of a dream in which he rode a dragon and was handed the royal cauldron. Hu further said that some at court were promoting a lineage traced to Prince Yuanzuo of Chu as the rightful succession—and that the man they meant was Zhonghong.

sentences.zh: 初，欲直書仲鴻名，同臺張孝伯見之曰：「書其名則竄矣。

translations.literal: At first they intended to write Zhonghong's name directly; fellow censor Zhang Xiaobo saw it and said: "Write his name and he will be banished.
translations.idiomatic: At first Hu meant to name Zhonghong outright. Fellow censor Zhang Xiaobo saw the draft and said, "Put his name in and he will be exiled.

sentences.zh: 凡阿附宰相，本冀官爵，此人沉埋六院且二年，心跡可察。

translations.literal: Those who fawn on the Chancellor generally hope for rank and title; this man has been buried in the Six Courts for nearly two years—his heart and conduct can be judged."
translations.idiomatic: Men who attach themselves to a chancellor usually want office and honors. This man has languished in the Six Courts for two years; his intentions are plain enough."

sentences.zh: 」卒不書其名。

translations.literal: In the end they did not write his name.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his name was left out.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年，汝愚罷相，仲鴻遷軍器監主簿，力丐外，除知洋州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingyuan, Ruyu was removed as Chancellor; Zhonghong was transferred to chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments, forcefully begged for an outer post, and was appointed prefect of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingyuan, after Ruyu was dismissed as chancellor, Zhonghong was moved to chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments; he pressed hard for a provincial post and was made prefect of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱熹聞其出，曰：「信蜀士之多奇也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi, hearing of his departure, said: "Truly the scholars of Shu produce many remarkable men.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi heard that he was being sent out, he said, "So it is true—Sichuan breeds extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 」越三年，起知嘉定府。

translations.literal: " Three years later he was recalled as prefect of Jiading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Three years on he was recalled to serve as prefect of Jiading.

sentences.zh: 擢利路轉運判官，數忤宣撫副使吳曦，曦言仲鴻老病，朝命易他部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Transport Commissioner of Liyu Circuit; he repeatedly offended Pacification Vice Commissioner Wu Xi; Xi said Zhonghong was old and ill, and the court ordered him transferred to another circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Transport Commissioner of Liyu Circuit, he clashed repeatedly with Pacification Vice Commissioner Wu Xi. Xi reported that Zhonghong was aged and infirm, and the court reassigned him elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 未幾，曦叛，宣撫司幕官薛紱訪仲鴻於果山，仲鴻對之泣，指案上一編書示紱曰：「開禧丁卯正月遊某死。

translations.literal: Not long after, Xi rebelled; staff officer Xue Fu of the Pacification Commission visited Zhonghong at Guo Mountain; Zhonghong wept before him, pointed to a bound book on the desk, and showed Fu, saying: "In the first month of dingmao in Kaixi, You So-and-so dies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xi rose in rebellion. Xue Fu, a staff officer of the Pacification Commission, came to see Zhonghong on Mount Guo. Zhonghong wept as he faced him, then pointed to a bound volume on his desk and showed it to Fu: "First month, dingmao year of Kaixi—You So-and-so dies.

sentences.zh: 」謂家人曰：「曦逼吾死，即填其日。」

translations.literal: " He told his family: "Xi is forcing my death—fill in that very date."
translations.idiomatic: " He told his household, "Xi is driving me to my death—when it happens, enter that very date."

sentences.zh: 時宣撫大使程松已棄其師遁，仲鴻以書勸成都帥楊輔討賊，輔不能用。

translations.literal: By then Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief Cheng Song had already abandoned his army and fled; Zhonghong wrote urging Chengdu commander Yang Fu to suppress the rebels, but Fu could not act on it.
translations.idiomatic: By then Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief Cheng Song had already deserted his troops and fled. Zhonghong wrote urging Chengdu commander Yang Fu to crush the rebels, but Fu would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 至是松至果，仲鴻謂紱曰：「宣威肯留，則吾以積奉二萬緡犒兵，護宣威之成都。

translations.literal: At this point Song arrived at Guo. Zhonghong said to Fu: "If Lord Xuanwei is willing to remain, then I will use twenty thousand strings of accumulated salary to reward the troops and escort Lord Xuanwei to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Song reached Guo, You Zhonghong told Xue Fu, "If the pacification commissioner will stay, I will spend twenty thousand strings of my saved stipend to reward the troops and escort him back to Chengdu."

sentences.zh: 」松不顧而去。

translations.literal: " Song paid no heed and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Song ignored the offer and left.

sentences.zh: 總賦劉崇之繼至，仲鴻遣其子似往見，以告松者告之，崇之復不聽。

translations.literal: Chief tax commissioner Liu Chongzhi arrived in succession. Zhonghong sent his son Si to call on him and told him what he had told Song; Chongzhi again would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The chief tax commissioner Liu Chongzhi came next. You Zhonghong sent his son You Si to see him and repeated the plea he had made to Cheng Song, but Liu Chongzhi would not listen either.

sentences.zh: 未幾，曦誅，參政李壁奏除利路提點刑獄，尋乞休致，予祠而歸，遷中奉大夫。

translations.literal: Before long Xi was executed. Grand Councilor Li Bi memorialized to appoint him Judicial Intendant for Li Circuit; soon he requested retirement, was granted a stipended temple post and returned home, and was promoted to Right Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Wu Xi was put to death. Grand Councilor Li Bi memorialized to appoint You Zhonghong Judicial Intendant for Li Circuit; he soon asked to retire, was given a stipended temple post and sent home, and was promoted to Right Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 嘉定八年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Jiading, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiading 8 (1215), at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 劉光祖表其隧道曰：「於乎！

translations.literal: Liu Guangzu composed an epitaph for his tomb passage, saying: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangzu wrote the inscription for his tomb passage: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 慶元黨人遊公之墓。

translations.literal: The Qingyuan faction members visit Lord You's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Members of the Qingyuan faction come to Lord You's grave.

sentences.zh: 」紹定五年，諡曰「忠」。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year of Shaoding, the posthumous title was "Loyal."
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding 5 (1232) he was given the posthumous title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子：似，淳祐五年為右丞相，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son: Si, who in the fifth year of Chunyou became Right Chancellor, has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son You Si became right chancellor in Chunyou 5 (1245) and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李祥，字元德，常州無錫人。

translations.literal: Li Xiang, styled Yuande, was a man of Wuxi in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang, courtesy name Yuande, was a native of Wuxi in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年進士，為錢塘縣主簿。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the first year of Longxing, he served as chief clerk of Qiantang County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Longxing 1 (1163) and served as chief clerk of Qiantang County.

sentences.zh: 時姚憲尹臨安，俾攝錄參。

translations.literal: At the time Yao Xian was prefect of Lin'an and had him act as Records Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xian was prefect of Lin'an, he had Li Xiang serve as acting Records Assistant.

sentences.zh: 邏者以巧發為能，每事下有司，必監視鍛煉，囚服乃已。

translations.literal: Runners regarded skillful arrests as merit; whenever a case was sent down to subordinate offices, they had to oversee torture until the prisoner confessed before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: The runners took clever arrests for ability; whenever a case was referred to a subordinate office, they insisted on supervising interrogation under torture until the prisoner confessed.

sentences.zh: 嘗誣告一武臣子謗朝政，鞫於獄，祥不使邏者入門。

translations.literal: Once a false accusation was made that a martial officer's son had slandered court affairs; he was tried in prison, and Xiang would not allow the runners to enter the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone falsely accused a military officer's son of slandering the government; when the case was tried in jail, Li Xiang refused to let the runners inside.

sentences.zh: 既而所告無實，具以白尹，尹驚曰：「上命無實乎？

translations.literal: When the accusation proved groundless, he reported the full facts to the prefect, who was alarmed and said: "Was the imperial order without basis?
translations.idiomatic: When the charge proved false, he reported everything to the prefect, who exclaimed, "So the imperial order had no basis?

sentences.zh: 」祥曰：「即坐譴，自甘。

translations.literal: " Xiang said: "Even if I am punished for it, I accept it willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang replied, "Even if I am punished for this, I accept it willingly."

sentences.zh: 」憲具論如祥意，上駭曰：「朕幾誤矣，卿吾爭臣也。

translations.literal: " Yao fully memorialized according to Xiang's view. The emperor was startled and said: "I nearly erred; you are my remonstrating minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xian memorialized in full accord with Li Xiang's position. The emperor was shaken and said, "I nearly made a mistake; you are my remonstrating minister."

sentences.zh: 」遂賜憲出身為諫大夫，祥調濠州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: " Yao was accordingly granted direct appointment as Remonstrance Grandee, and Xiang was transferred to Records Assistant in Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xian was then granted direct appointment as Remonstrance Grandee, and Li Xiang was transferred to Records Assistant in Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 安豐守臣冒占民田，訟屢改而不決，監司委祥，卒歸之民。

translations.literal: The prefect of Anfeng had illegally seized civilian land; the lawsuit was repeatedly reassigned without resolution. The supervisory official entrusted Xiang, and in the end the land was restored to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Anfeng had illegally occupied civilian fields; the lawsuit was repeatedly reassigned without a decision. The supervisory official put the case in Li Xiang's hands, and he finally returned the land to its owners.

sentences.zh: 未幾，其人易守濠，以嫌換司理廬州；

translations.literal: Before long that man was transferred to be prefect of Haozhou; because of the conflict of interest, Xiang was reassigned as judicial officer in Luzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Before long that official became prefect of Haozhou; because of the conflict of interest, Li Xiang was transferred to serve as judicial officer in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 守出改官奏留之，不可。

translations.literal: the prefect submitted a memorial recommending him for promotion and asking to retain him; this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect submitted a memorial to promote him and keep him in post, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 主管戶部架閣文字、太學博士、國子博士、司農寺丞、樞密院編脩官兼刑部郎官、大宗正丞、軍器少監。

translations.literal: He served as Supervisor of Ministry of Revenue Archival Documents, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Erudite of the National University, Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, Compilation Officer of the Privy Council and concurrently Official of the Ministry of Justice, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Vice Director of the Armaments Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of supervisor of Ministry of Revenue archival documents, erudite of the Imperial Academy, erudite of the National University, vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture, privy council compilation officer with concurrent appointment in the Ministry of Justice, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, and vice director of the Armaments Directorate.

sentences.zh: 言：「忝朝跡八年，在外賢才不勝眾，願更出迭入由臣始。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Having disgraced the court trail for eight years, outstanding talent outside exceeds those within; I wish that rotation between inside and outside service begin with me.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "I have held a place at court for eight years, yet worthy men outside still far outnumber those within; let the practice of moving in and out of office begin with me."

sentences.zh: 」出提舉淮東常平茶鹽、淮西運判。

translations.literal: " He was sent out as Intendant of Huaidong Ever-normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt, and as Transport Vice Commissioner of Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed intendant of Huaidong ever-normal granaries, tea, and salt, and transport vice commissioner for Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 兩淮鐵錢比不定，祥疏乞官賜錢米銷濫惡者，廢定城、興國、漢陽監，更鑄紹熙新錢，從之，淮人以安。

translations.literal: Iron cash in the two Huai regions had long been unstable. Xiang memorialized requesting that the government grant cash and grain to redeem inferior and counterfeit coins, abolish the mints at Dingcheng, Xingguo, and Hanyang, and recast new Shaoxi coins. The request was approved, and the people of the Huai region were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Iron cash in the two Huai regions had long been unstable. Li Xiang memorialized asking the government to issue official cash and grain to buy up inferior and debased coin, abolish the mints at Dingcheng, Xingguo, and Hanyang, and recast new Shaoxi currency. The court agreed, and the Huai region was calmed.

sentences.zh: 遷國子司業、宗正少卿、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Rector of the National University, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice rector of the National University, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, and chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 丞相趙汝愚以言去國，祥上疏爭之，曰：「頃壽皇崩，兩宮隔絕，中外洶洶，留正棄印亡去，國命如𩬊。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Zhao Ruyu was removed from office because of a memorial, Xiang submitted a memorial protesting, saying: "Recently, when Emperor Xiaozong died, the two palaces were cut off from one another and court and countryside were in uproar; Liu Zheng cast aside his seal and fled, and the fate of the state hung by a hair.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Zhao Ruyu was driven from office after a memorial attack, Li Xiang submitted a protest, saying, "When Emperor Xiaozong died not long ago, the two palaces were cut off from each other and the realm was in turmoil; Liu Zheng abandoned his seal and fled, and the nation's fate hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 汝愚不畏滅族，決策立陛下，風塵不搖，天下復安，社稷之臣也。

translations.literal: Ruyu did not fear extermination of his clan, resolved to establish Your Majesty, the dust of turmoil did not shake, and the realm was restored to peace — he is a minister of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu did not fear the destruction of his whole clan, decided to enthrone Your Majesty, kept the realm steady through the crisis, and brought the empire back to peace — he is a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 奈何無念功至意，忽體貌常典，使精忠巨節怫鬱黯闇，何以示後世？」

translations.literal: How can you fail to remember his utmost merit, suddenly neglect the usual honors due his stature, and leave great loyalty and towering integrity sullen and obscured — what will this show posterity?"
translations.idiomatic: Why forget his supreme service, abruptly withhold the honors normally owed a man of his stature, and leave towering loyalty and integrity buried in resentment and obscurity? What lesson is that for posterity?"

sentences.zh: 除直龍圖閣、湖南運副，言者劾罷之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall and Transport Vice Commissioner of Hunan; memorializers impeached him and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed directly attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall and transport vice commissioner for Hunan, but critics impeached him and he was removed.

sentences.zh: 於是太學諸生楊宏中、周端朝等六人上書留之，俱得罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon six Imperial University students, including Yang Hongzhong and Zhou Duanchao, submitted a joint memorial asking that he be retained; all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Six Imperial University students, including Yang Hongzhong and Zhou Duanchao, then submitted a joint memorial asking that he be kept in office; all were punished.

sentences.zh: 主沖佑觀，再請老，以直龍圖閣致仕。

translations.literal: He was put in charge of Chongyou Temple; again requesting retirement, he retired with the rank of Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in charge of Chongyou Temple; after again requesting retirement, he retired with the rank of directly attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰元年八月卒，諡「肅簡」。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth month of the first year of Jiatai; his posthumous title was "Solemn and Simple."
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Jiatai 1 (1201) and was given the posthumous title Solemn and Simple.

sentences.zh: 簽書昭慶軍節度判官廳公事，除為國子錄，上疏言：「壽皇親挈神器授之陛下，孝敬豈可久闕乎？

translations.literal: Signing Secretary of the Zhaoping Military Circuit Commissioner's office; appointed Registrar of the National University; he submitted a memorial saying: "Emperor Xiaozong personally handed the sacred vessel to Your Majesty — how can filial reverence be long neglected?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie served as signing secretary in the Zhaoping military commissioner's office and was appointed registrar of the National University. He memorialized, "Emperor Xiaozong personally entrusted the imperial regalia to Your Majesty — how can filial duty be neglected for long?

sentences.zh: 」又言：「婦事舅姑如事父母，不可虧宮中之禮。

translations.literal: " He also said: "A wife serves her parents-in-law as she serves her parents; the rites of the inner palace must not be diminished.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "A wife serves her parents-in-law as she serves her own parents; the ceremonial obligations of the inner palace must not be slighted."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，介又力請上過宮執喪，累疏言辭激切，人歎其忠。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died, Jie again strongly urged the emperor to go to the inner palace to observe mourning; he repeatedly memorialized with incisive language, and people praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, Wang Jie again pressed the emperor to go to the inner palace to observe mourning; his repeated memorials were sharp and impassioned, and people admired his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，介上疏言：「陛下即位未三月，策免宰相，遷易臺諫，悉出內批，非治世事也。

translations.literal: When Ningzong ascended the throne, Jie submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has been on the throne less than three months, yet you have dismissed the chancellor by edict, replaced censors and remonstrators, and all of this has come from inner drafts — this is not the way to govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong took the throne, Wang Jie memorialized, "Your Majesty has reigned less than three months, yet you have removed the chancellor by edict, reshuffled the censorate and remonstrance bureau, and all of it has issued from inner drafts — this is no way to run the state.

sentences.zh: 崇寧、大觀間事出御批，遂成北狩之禍。

translations.literal: Between Chongning and Daguan, affairs issued from imperial drafts and thus brought about the disaster of the northern flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongning and Daguan periods, government by imperial draft led to the catastrophe of the flight north.

sentences.zh: 杜衍為相，常積內降十數封還，今宰相不敢封納，臺諫不敢彈奏，此豈可久之道。

translations.literal: When Du Yan was chancellor, he regularly accumulated more than ten inner edicts and returned them sealed; now the chancellor dares not seal and return them, and the censorate and remonstrators dare not impeach — can such a course endure?
translations.idiomatic: When Du Yan was chancellor, he would regularly accumulate a dozen inner edicts and send them back sealed; now the chancellor does not dare seal and return them, and the censorate and remonstrators do not dare impeach — can this go on?

sentences.zh: 」遷太學博士。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 時韓侂胄居中潛弄威福之柄，猶未肆也，而文墨議論之士陰附之以希進，於是始無所憚矣。

translations.literal: At the time Han Tuozhou held power at court and secretly manipulated authority and favor; he had not yet become unrestrained, but literary and debating scholars secretly attached themselves to him hoping for advancement, and only then did he begin to fear nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Tuozhou dominated the court and secretly wielded power and patronage; he had not yet fully thrown off restraint, but men of letters and debate quietly attached themselves to him in hope of promotion, and only then did he begin to act without fear.

sentences.zh: 侂胄始疑介前封事詆己，且其弟仰胄嘗以舊識求自通，介拒絕之，侂胄怨益深。

translations.literal: Tuozhou began to suspect that Jie's earlier sealed memorial had slandered him, and moreover his younger brother Yangzhou had once sought contact through an old acquaintance; Jie refused him, and Tuozhou's resentment grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou came to suspect that Wang Jie's earlier sealed memorial had attacked him, and when his younger brother Han Yangzhou once tried to renew an old acquaintance, Wang Jie refused him; Han Tuozhou's resentment deepened.

sentences.zh: 添差通判紹興府，尋知邵武軍。

translations.literal: He was given an additional assignment as vice prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture, and soon became prefect of Shaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He received an additional appointment as vice prefect of Shaoxing, and soon became prefect of Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 會學禁起，諫大夫姚愈劾介與袁燮皆偽學之黨，且附會前相汝愚，主管台州崇道觀。

translations.literal: When the Learning Proscription arose, Remonstrance Grandee Yao Yu impeached Jie and Yuan Xie as both members of the pseud-learning faction and as attached to the former chancellor Ruyu; Jie was put in charge of Chongdao Temple in Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Learning Proscription began, Remonstrance Grandee Yao Yu impeached Wang Jie and Yuan Xie as members of the pseud-learning faction and as allies of the former chancellor Zhao Ruyu; Wang Jie was placed in charge of Chongdao Temple in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，差知廣德軍。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was assigned as prefect of Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was assigned as prefect of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 侂胄之隸人蘇師旦忿介不通謁，目為偽黨，並及甲寅廷對之語，以告侂胄。

translations.literal: Tuozhou's servant Su Shidan resented that Jie did not pay court visits, labeled him a member of the pseud-learning faction, and also included remarks from the jiayin court audience, reporting this to Tuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou's retainer Su Shidan, angry that Wang Jie would not call on him, denounced him as a pseud-learning partisan and added charges drawn from Wang Jie's jiayin palace examination answers, then reported all of this to Han Tuozhou.

sentences.zh: 有勸其自明者，介曰：「吾髮已種種，豈為鼠輩所使邪！

translations.literal: Some advised him to clear himself; Jie said: "My hair is already sparse and white — would I be driven by vermin!
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to defend himself. Wang Jie said, "My hair is already thin and white — am I to be pushed around by rats?

sentences.zh: 」侂胄亦畏公議不敢發。

translations.literal: " Tuozhou also feared public opinion and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou also feared public opinion and did not dare move against him.

sentences.zh: 以外艱去。

translations.literal: He left office because of mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 免喪，知饒州，未赴，召為秘書郎，遷度支郎官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was made prefect of Raozhou; before he went, he was summoned as Secretary of the Secretariat and transferred to Bureau Officer in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was appointed prefect of Raozhou. Before he took up the post, he was recalled as Secretary of the Secretariat and promoted to bureau officer in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 師旦已建節，介與同列謁政府，遇之於庭，客皆逾階而揖，介不顧。

translations.literal: Shidan had already established a command seal. Jie and colleagues of the same rank visited the chief councilors' office and met him in the courtyard; the guests all crossed the steps to bow, but Jie paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Shidan had already been granted a command seal. When Jie and his colleagues paid a call at the chief councilors' office, they encountered him in the courtyard; the other guests all crossed the steps to bow, but Jie took no notice.

sentences.zh: 於是殿中侍御史徐柟劾介資淺立異，奉祠，除都大坑冶。

translations.literal: Thereupon Palace Attendant Censor Xu Nan impeached Jie for shallow qualifications and standing apart in contrariness. He was granted a ceremonial sinecure and appointed Commissioner for Mining and Minting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Palace Attendant Censor Xu Nan impeached Jie for shallow qualifications and deliberate contrariness. He was granted a ceremonial sinecure and appointed Commissioner for Mining and Minting Affairs.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，朝廷更化，介召還，除侍左郎官兼右司、太子舍人，改兵部郎官、國子司業、太子侍講兼國史院編修官、實錄院檢討官，除國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Tuozhou was executed and the court changed course, Jie was recalled. He was appointed Left Attendant in the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently Right Division and Crown Prince Attendant; transferred to Bureau Officer in the Ministry of War, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, Crown Prince Lecturer concurrent Compiler in the Historical Compilation Office and Reviewer in the Veritable Records Office; and appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Tuozhou was executed and the court changed course, Jie was recalled. He was appointed Left Attendant in the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently serving in the Right Division and as Crown Prince Attendant; then transferred to bureau officer in the Ministry of War, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, Crown Prince Lecturer concurrent compiler in the Historical Compilation Office and reviewer in the Veritable Records Office; and finally appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 會以不雨，詔百官指陳闕失，時宰相史彌遠以母喪起復，介手疏歷論時政，推本《洪範》僭恒暘若之證，謂：「羅日愿為變，是下人謀上也。

translations.literal: There happened to be drought, and an edict ordered all officials to point out faults and oversights. At the time Grand Counselor Shi Miyuan returned to duty from mourning for his mother. Jie submitted a handwritten memorial reviewing current policy in detail, tracing the evidence to the omen in the "Great Plan" that usurpation brings constant drought, saying: "When Luo Riyuan plotted rebellion, that was subordinates scheming against their superiors.
translations.idiomatic: There happened to be a drought, and an edict called on all officials to point out faults and oversights. At the time Grand Counselor Shi Miyuan had returned to duty from mourning for his mother before the mourning period was complete. Jie submitted a handwritten memorial reviewing current policy in detail, tracing the evidence to the omen in the "Great Plan" that usurpation brings constant drought, and said: "When Luo Riyuan plotted rebellion, that was subordinates scheming against their superiors.

sentences.zh: 修好增幣，而金人猶觖望，是夷人亂華也。

translations.literal: We restored friendly relations and increased tribute, yet the Jurchen still harbor grievances—that is barbarians disturbing China.
translations.idiomatic: We restored friendly relations and increased tribute payments, yet the Jurchen still harbor grievances—that is barbarians disturbing China.

sentences.zh: 內批數出，是左右干政也。

translations.literal: Palace directives issue one after another—that is attendants interfering in government.
translations.idiomatic: Palace directives issue one after another—that is attendants interfering in government.

sentences.zh: 諫官無故出省，是小人間君子也。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials leave the capital for no reason—that is petty men sowing discord against gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials leave the capital for no reason—that is petty men sowing discord against gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 皆謂之僭。

translations.literal: All these are called usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: All of these are usurpation.

sentences.zh: 一僭已足以致天變，而況兼有之哉。

translations.literal: A single act of usurpation is enough to bring heaven's wrath—how much more when all are present together!
translations.idiomatic: A single act of usurpation is enough to bring heaven's wrath—how much more when all are present at once!

sentences.zh: 」又言：「漢法天地降災，策免丞相，乞令彌遠終喪，擇公正無私者置左右，王、呂、蔡、秦之覆轍，可以為戒。」

translations.literal: He also said: "By Han precedent, when heaven and earth send down disaster, the Grand Counselor is removed by edict. I beg that Miyuan be allowed to complete his mourning, that upright and impartial men be placed at Your Majesty's side, and that the overturned chariots of Wang, Lü, Cai, and Qin serve as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "By Han precedent, when heaven and earth send down disaster, the chief minister is removed by edict. I beg that Miyuan be allowed to complete his mourning, that upright and impartial men be placed at Your Majesty's side, and that the overturned chariots of Wang, Lü, Cai, and Qin serve as a warning."

sentences.zh: 接送伴金國賀生辰使還，奏：「故事兩國通廟諱、御名，而本朝止通御名，高宗至光宗皆傳名而不傳諱，紹熙初，黃裳嘗以為言，而未及釐正。

translations.literal: After escorting the Jin envoy who had come to congratulate the emperor's birthday back to the border, he memorialized: "By precedent the two states exchanged both temple taboo names and imperial personal names, but our dynasty exchanges only personal names. From Gaozong through Guangzong only personal names were transmitted, not taboo names. Early in the Shaoxi reign Huang Shang raised the point, but the rite was never corrected.
translations.idiomatic: After escorting the Jin envoy who had come to congratulate the emperor's birthday back to the border, he memorialized: "By precedent the two states exchanged both temple taboo names and imperial personal names, but our dynasty exchanges only personal names. From Gaozong through Guangzong only personal names were transmitted, not taboo names. Early in the Shaoxi reign Huang Shang raised the point, but the rite was never corrected.

sentences.zh: 願正典禮，以尊宗廟。」

translations.literal: I wish that the canonical rites be set right, to honor the imperial ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: I wish that the canonical rites be set right, to honor the imperial ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 除秘書監，升太子右諭德。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat and promoted to Right Mentor of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat and promoted to Right Mentor of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 其在春宮，篤意輔導，每遇講讀，因事規諫。

translations.literal: While serving in the Eastern Palace, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to instruction; whenever lectures and readings were held, he admonished on whatever occasion offered.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Eastern Palace, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to instruction; whenever lectures and readings were held, he admonished the crown prince on whatever occasion offered.

sentences.zh: 太子嘗欲索館中圖畫，卻而弗與，及張燈設樂，則諫止之；

translations.literal: The crown prince once wished to claim paintings from the library pavilion; Jie refused. When lamps were lit and music arranged, he remonstrated and stopped it;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince once wished to claim paintings from the library pavilion; Jie refused. When lamps were lit and music arranged, he remonstrated and stopped it;

sentences.zh: 且乞選配故家以正始，絕令旨以杜請謁，宮僚分日上直，以資見聞。

translations.literal: He further requested that matches be chosen from established families to set a proper beginning, that imperial orders be cut off to block solicitations, and that palace staff take turns on daily duty so as to broaden experience.
translations.idiomatic: He further requested that matches be chosen from established families to set a proper beginning, that imperial orders be cut off to block solicitations, and that palace staff take turns on daily duty so as to broaden the crown prince's experience.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正少卿兼權中書舍人，繳駁不避權貴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, acting concurrently as Drafting Secretary, returning drafts with objections without fear of the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, acting concurrently as Drafting Secretary, returning drafts with objections without fear of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 張允濟以閣職為州鈐，介謂此小事而用權臣例，破祖宗制，不可不封還詞頭。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunji was given a pavilion appointment as military controller of a prefecture. Jie said that though the matter was minor, to use a precedent set by powerful ministers would break ancestral institutions—it could not but be met by returning the appointment draft.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunji was given a pavilion appointment as military controller of a prefecture. Jie said that though the matter was minor, to use a precedent set by powerful ministers would break ancestral institutions—the appointment draft had to be returned.

sentences.zh: 丞相語介曰：「此中宮意。

translations.literal: The Grand Counselor told Jie, "This is the empress's wish."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Counselor told Jie, "This is the empress's wish."

sentences.zh: 」介曰：「宰相而逢宮禁意向，給舍而奉宰相風旨，朝廷紀綱掃地矣。」

translations.literal: Jie said, "If the Grand Counselor follows the wishes of the palace women, and the drafting secretaries follow the Grand Counselor's lead, the discipline of court and state is swept clean away."
translations.idiomatic: Jie replied, "If the Grand Counselor follows the wishes of the palace women, and the drafting secretaries follow the Grand Counselor's lead, the discipline of court and state is swept clean away."

sentences.zh: 居數日，除起居舍人。

translations.literal: Several days later he was appointed Recorder of the Emperor's Acts.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he was appointed Recorder of the Emperor's Acts.

sentences.zh: 介奏：「宰相以私請不行，而託威福於宮禁，權且下移，誰敢以忠告陛下者。

translations.literal: Jie memorialized: "The Grand Counselor's private request was not granted, so he entrusted authority to the palace women and power shifted downward—who would dare speak frankly to advise Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Jie memorialized: "The Grand Counselor's private request was not granted, so he entrusted authority to the palace women and power shifted downward—who would dare speak frankly to advise Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 」乞歸老，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to retire, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to retire, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 言：「本朝循唐入閤之制，左右史不立前殿，若御後殿，則立朵殿下，何所聞見而修起居注乎？

translations.literal: He said: "Our dynasty follows the Tang system of entering the inner hall; the Left and Right Historians are not stationed in the front hall. If the emperor holds court in the rear hall, they stand beneath the bracket ceiling—what can they hear and see by which to compile the record of the emperor's acts?"
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Our dynasty follows the Tang system of entering the inner hall; the Left and Right Historians are not stationed in the front hall. If the emperor holds court in the rear hall, they stand beneath the bracket ceiling—what can they hear and see by which to compile the record of the emperor's acts?"

sentences.zh: 乞依歐陽修、王存、胡銓所請，分立殿上。」

translations.literal: I beg that, following the requests of Ouyang Xiu, Wang Cun, and Hu Quan, they be stationed separately within the hall."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that, following the requests of Ouyang Xiu, Wang Cun, and Hu Quan, they be stationed separately within the hall."

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎許奕以言事去國，介奏曰：「陛下更化三年，而言事官去者五人，倪思、傅伯成既去，其後蔡幼學、鄒應龍相繼而出，今許奕復蹈前轍。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Yi left office for having remonstrated. Jie memorialized: "Your Majesty has changed course for three years, yet five remonstrance officials have departed—Ni Si and Fu Bocheng left first; afterward Cai Youxue and Zou Yinglong left in succession; and now Xu Yi follows the same path.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Yi left office for having remonstrated. Jie memorialized: "Your Majesty has changed course for three years, yet five remonstrance officials have departed—Ni Si and Fu Bocheng left first; afterward Cai Youxue and Zou Yinglong left in succession; and now Xu Yi follows the same path.

sentences.zh: 此五臣者，四為給事，一為諫大夫，兩年之間，盡聽其去。

translations.literal: Of these five ministers, four were drafting officials and one was Grand Remonstrance Counselor; within two years Your Majesty allowed them all to go.
translations.idiomatic: Of these five ministers, four were drafting officials and one was Grand Remonstrance Counselor; within two years Your Majesty allowed them all to go.

sentences.zh: 或謂此皆宰相意，自古未有大臣因給舍論事而去之者，是大臣誤陛下也，將恐成孤立之勢。

translations.literal: Some say this is all at the Grand Counselor's wish. Never before has a chief minister departed because drafting officials remonstrated—the chief minister is misleading Your Majesty, and I fear an isolated situation will result.
translations.idiomatic: Some say this is all at the Grand Counselor's wish. Never before has a chief minister departed because drafting officials remonstrated—the chief minister is misleading Your Majesty, and I fear an isolated situation will result.

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，乞補外，以右文殿修撰知嘉興府。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted he requested an outside appointment and was made Compiler at the Youwen Hall and prefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted he requested an outside appointment and was made Compiler at the Youwen Hall and prefect of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，升集英殿修撰、知襄陽府、京西安撫使。

translations.literal: More than a year later he was promoted to Compiler at the Jiying Hall, prefect of Xiangyang, and Pacification Commissioner of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was promoted to Compiler at the Jiying Hall, prefect of Xiangyang, and Pacification Commissioner of Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 徙知慶元府兼沿海製置使，以疾奉祠。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Qingyuan and Coastal Defense Commissioner; due to illness he was granted a ceremonial sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Qingyuan and Coastal Defense Commissioner; due to illness he was granted a ceremonial sinecure.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年八月卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Jiading he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixth year of Jiading he died, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 端平三年，郡守趙汝談請於朝，特贈中大夫、寶章閣待制，諡「忠簡」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping the prefect Zhao Rutang petitioned the court, and Jie was posthumously granted the title of Middle Court Grandee and Awaiting Orders at the Baozhang Hall, with the posthumous name "Loyal and Simple."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duanping the prefect Zhao Rutang petitioned the court, and Jie was posthumously granted the title of Middle Court Grandee and Awaiting Orders at the Baozhang Hall, with the posthumous name "Loyal and Simple."

sentences.zh: 子：野，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son: Ye, who has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son: Ye, who has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 宋德之

translations.literal: Song Dezhi
translations.idiomatic: Song Dezhi

sentences.zh: 宋德之，字正仲，其先京兆人。

translations.literal: Song Dezhi, styled Zhenghong, was originally from Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Song Dezhi, whose courtesy name was Zhenghong, came from Jingzhao by ancestry.

sentences.zh: 隋諫大夫遠謫彭山，子孫散居於蜀，遂為蜀州人。

translations.literal: In the Sui, Remonstrance Counselor Yuan was exiled to Pengshan; his descendants scattered through Shu and became natives of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Sui dynasty Remonstrance Counselor Yuan was exiled to Pengshan; his descendants scattered through Shu and became natives of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 德之以應舉擢慶元二年外省第一，為山南道掌書記。

translations.literal: Dezhi placed first in the provincial examination in the second year of Qingyuan and was made secretary of Shannan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhi placed first in the provincial examination in the second year of Qingyuan and was made secretary of Shannan circuit.

sentences.zh: 召除國子正，遷武學博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education, then transferred to Erudite of the Military Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education, then transferred to Erudite of the Military Academy.

sentences.zh: 與諸生論八陣之象本乎八卦，皆動物也，奇正之變，往來相生而不窮，知此然後可以致勝。

translations.literal: With the students he discussed how the images of the Eight Formations derive from the Eight Trigrams—all are animate beings; the changes of odd and even formations, coming and going, generate one another without end. Only knowing this can one achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: With the students he discussed how the images of the Eight Formations derive from the Eight Trigrams—all are animate forms; the changes of odd and even deployments, coming and going, generate one another without end. Only with this knowledge can one achieve victory.

sentences.zh: 遷編修樞密院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時兵釁有萌，會赤眚見太陰，犯權星，未浹日，內北門鴟尾災，延及三省、六部，詔求言，德之奏：「離為火，為日，為甲胄；

translations.literal: At the time signs of military trouble were emerging; a red omen appeared on the moon and invaded the Regulator star. Before a full day had passed, fire struck the Inner North Gate at the roof finials and spread to the Three Departments and Six Ministries. An edict solicited opinion. Dezhi memorialized: "Li signifies fire, the sun, and armor;
translations.idiomatic: At the time signs of military trouble were emerging; a red omen appeared on the moon and invaded the Regulator star. Before a full day had passed, fire struck the Inner North Gate at the roof finials and spread to the Three Departments and Six Ministries. An edict solicited opinion. Dezhi memorialized: "Li signifies fire, the sun, and armor;

sentences.zh: 坎為水，為月，為盜，為隱伏。

translations.literal: Kan signifies water, the moon, brigands, and hidden plots.
translations.idiomatic: Kan signifies water, the moon, brigands, and hidden plots.

sentences.zh: 故火失其性，赤氣見，憂在甲兵；

translations.literal: Thus when fire loses its nature, red vapors appear—sorrow lies in armed conflict;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when fire loses its nature, red vapors appear—the concern lies in armed conflict;

sentences.zh: 水失其性，太陰失度，憂在隱伏。

translations.literal: when water loses its nature, the moon departs from its measure—sorrow lies in hidden plots."
translations.idiomatic: when water loses its nature, the moon departs from its measure—the concern lies in hidden plots."

sentences.zh: 」因疏七事，皆當今至切之患，乃曰：「人火小變不足慮，天象之變，臣竊危之。」

translations.literal: He then memorialized on seven matters, all among the most pressing ills of the day, and said: "Human fire is a minor change and not worth worry; the change in the heavenly signs—I venture to say—fills me with dread."
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized on seven matters, all among the most pressing ills of the day, and said: "Human fire is a minor change and not worth worry; the change in the heavenly signs—I venture to say—fills me with dread."

sentences.zh: 他日，又對曰：「今敵未動，而輕變祖宗舊制，命武臣帥邊以自遺患。

translations.literal: On another day he addressed the throne again: "The enemy has not yet moved, yet we lightly alter our ancestors' old institutions and appoint military men to command the borders, inviting disaster upon ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he addressed the throne again: "The enemy has not yet moved, yet we lightly alter our ancestors' old institutions and appoint military men to command the borders, inviting disaster upon ourselves.

sentences.zh: 晉叛將、唐藩鎮之禍基於此矣。

translations.literal: The disaster of the Jin defector general and the Tang military governors took root in just this."
translations.idiomatic: The disaster of the Jin defector general and the Tang military governors took root in just this."

sentences.zh: 」時吳曦在西陲，皇甫斌在襄漢，郭倪、李爽在兩淮，德之預以為慮。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Xi was on the western frontier, Huangfu Bin in the Xiang and Han region, and Guo Ni and Li Shuang on the Two Huai—Dezhi had already regarded them with foreboding.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Xi was on the western frontier, Huangfu Bin in the Xiang and Han region, and Guo Ni and Li Shuang on the Two Huai—Dezhi had already regarded them with foreboding.

sentences.zh: 除太常丞，出知閬州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of Court Ceremonies and sent out as prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of Court Ceremonies and sent out as prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 會曦變，託跌足以避偽，事平，始赴閬。

translations.literal: When Xi's rebellion broke out, he feigned lameness to avoid serving the puppet regime; after the affair was settled, he finally went to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi's rebellion broke out, he feigned lameness to avoid serving the puppet regime; after the affair was settled, he finally went to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢本路提點刑獄，制帥安丙奏：「德之傲視君命，不俟代者之來，徑用觀察使印領事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to judicial intendant for the circuit; the military commissioner An Bing memorialized: "Dezhi looked down on the sovereign's command, and without waiting for his successor to arrive, directly used the surveillance commissioner's seal to conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhi was promoted to judicial intendant of the circuit, whereupon the military commissioner An Bing submitted a memorial: "Dezhi has treated the imperial command with contempt; without waiting for his replacement to arrive, he took the surveillance commissioner's seal and assumed charge of affairs on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 」詔降一官，改潼川路轉運判官、湖南路提刑，改湖北。

translations.literal: " An edict demoted him one rank and reassigned him as transport vice-commissioner of the Tongchuan circuit and judicial intendant of the Hunan circuit, then changed him to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: " The court ordered him demoted one rank, reassigned him as transport vice-commissioner on the Tongchuan circuit and judicial intendant on the Hunan circuit, and then transferred him to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 召為兵部郎官。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed a department official in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed a department official in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 朝論有疑安丙意，丞相史彌遠首以問德之，德之對曰：「蜀無安丙，朝廷無蜀矣，人有大功，實不敢以私嫌廢公議。

translations.literal: Court opinion harbored doubts about An Bing's intentions, and the chief councilor Shi Miyuan was the first to put the question to Dezhi; Dezhi replied: "Without An Bing, Shu would have no defender, and the court would have no Shu; when a man has rendered great service, I truly dare not let private resentment overturn public judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Some at court suspected An Bing's motives, and Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan was the first to raise the matter with Dezhi. Dezhi answered: "Without An Bing there is no Shu, and without Shu the court has lost the west; when a man has done great service, I cannot allow private grievance to override the public good.

sentences.zh: 」忤時相意，遂罷。

translations.literal: " This ran counter to the chief councilor's wishes, and he was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " His answer offended the chief councilor, and he was promptly removed from office.

sentences.zh: 安丙深感德之，嘗謂人曰：「丙不知正仲，正仲知丙；

translations.literal: An Bing was deeply moved by Dezhi and once said to others: "Bing did not understand Zhengzhong, but Zhengzhong understood Bing;
translations.idiomatic: An Bing was deeply grateful to Dezhi and once told others: "Bing failed to know Zhengzhong, yet Zhengzhong knew Bing;

sentences.zh: 丙負正仲，正仲不負丙。

translations.literal: Bing wronged Zhengzhong, but Zhengzhong did not wrong Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Bing wronged Zhengzhong, but Zhengzhong never wronged Bing.

sentences.zh: 」請昏於德之，不許。

translations.literal: " He requested a marriage alliance with Dezhi, but permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked to form a marriage tie with Dezhi's family, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 論者益稱德之之賢。

translations.literal: Commentators all the more praised Dezhi's worth.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised Dezhi's integrity all the more.

sentences.zh: 起知眉州，監特奏名試，得疾而卒。

translations.literal: He was reappointed prefect of Meizhou, supervised the special examination for specially nominated candidates, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed prefect of Meizhou and put in charge of the special examination for specially nominated candidates; he took ill there and died.

sentences.zh: 德之大父耕，性剛介，一朝棄官去，莫知所終。

translations.literal: Dezhi's great-grandfather Geng was by nature stern and upright; one morning he abandoned his office and left, and no one knew his end.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhi's great-grandfather Geng was a man of stern integrity; one day he resigned his post and vanished, and none ever learned his fate.

sentences.zh: 從父廉語德之曰：「吾昔至臨安府，有人言蜀有宋宣教者過浙江而去，吾適越求之，則入四明矣。

translations.literal: His uncle's son Lian said to Dezhi: "When I once reached Lin'an Prefecture, someone said that in Shu there was a Song Xuanjiao who had crossed the Zhe River and gone on; I went to Yue to seek him, and he had entered Siming.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Lian told Dezhi: "When I was once in Lin'an, I heard that a man from Shu named Song Xuanjiao had crossed the Zhe River and traveled on. I went to Yue to look for him and learned he had gone on into Siming.

sentences.zh: 」德之渡浙江尋訪，至雪竇，有蜀僧言：「聞諸耆老云：山後有爛平山，有三居士焉，其一宋宣教也。

translations.literal: " Dezhi crossed the Zhe River to search; reaching Xuedou, a monk from Shu said: "I have heard the elders say that behind the mountain is Lanping Mountain, where three lay devotees dwell, one of whom is Song Xuanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: " Dezhi crossed the Zhe River in search of him. At Xuedou a Sichuan monk said: "The old men tell of Lanping Mountain behind the peak, where three lay devotees live—one of them is Song Xuanjiao.

sentences.zh: 」德之躋攀至爛平，見丹竈，置祠其上而歸。

translations.literal: " Dezhi climbed to Lanping, saw a cinnabar furnace, set up a shrine over it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Dezhi climbed to Lanping, found a cinnabar furnace, erected a shrine on the spot, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 楊大全

translations.literal: Yang Daquan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Daquan

sentences.zh: 楊大全，字渾甫，眉之青神人。

translations.literal: Yang Daquan, style name Hunfu, was a native of Qingshen in Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Daquan, courtesy name Hunfu, came from Qingshen in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道八年進士，調溫江尉，攝邑有政聲。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as magistrate of Wenjiang, and while acting as prefect earned a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the eighth year of the Qiandao reign and was appointed magistrate of Wenjiang; while serving in an acting prefectural capacity he won a name for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 紹熙三年，召除監登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxi he was summoned and removed to serve as superintendent of the Petition Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shaoxi he was recalled and appointed superintendent of the Petition Drum Court.

sentences.zh: 五年，光宗以疾久，不克省重華宮，廷臣多論諫者。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Emperor Guangzong, long afflicted by illness, was unable to visit Chonghua Palace; many court officials offered remonstrance and admonition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Emperor Guangzong had been ill for a long time and could not visit Chonghua Palace; many officials at court spoke out in remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 太學生汪安仁等二百餘人上書，而龔日章等百餘人以投匭上書為緩，必欲伏闕。

translations.literal: More than two hundred Imperial University students led by Wang Anren submitted memorials, while more than a hundred led by Gong Rizhang regarded submitting memorials through the suggestion box as too slow and insisted on prostrating themselves at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred Imperial University students, led by Wang Anren, submitted memorials, while another hundred-odd, led by Gong Rizhang, thought depositing petitions in the suggestion box too slow and insisted on kneeling at the palace gate instead.

sentences.zh: 大全謂：「院以登聞名，實明目達聰之地也，今乃使人視為具文，吾何顏以尸此職。

translations.literal: Daquan said: "This court is named for 'petitioning to be heard'; in truth it is the place where the sovereign's eyes are opened and his ears attuned—yet now people are made to treat it as empty formality; with what face can I hold this post in name alone?
translations.idiomatic: Daquan said: "This office is called the court where petitions reach the throne—it is meant to open the sovereign's eyes and ears. Yet now people treat it as a mere formality. How can I keep occupying the post without doing its work?

sentences.zh: 」乃為書以諫，力請過宮，書上不報。

translations.literal: " He thereupon wrote a memorial to remonstrate, urgently requesting that the emperor visit the palace; the memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote a memorial urging the emperor to visit the palace. The memorial was submitted, but no answer came.

sentences.zh: 大全於是三上疏，其略曰：

translations.literal: Daquan thereupon submitted three further memorials; the gist read:
translations.idiomatic: Daquan then submitted three more memorials. The substance was as follows:

sentences.zh: 「臣之志於憂君者，不畏義死，不榮幸生，不以言而獲罪為恥，而以言不聽從為恥。

translations.literal: "In one who sets his will on grieving for his lord, I do not fear dying for righteousness, do not count it glory to live by favor, do not take being punished for words as shame, but take having one's words go unheeded as shame.
translations.idiomatic: "As one who grieves for his sovereign, I do not fear a righteous death, do not prize a life of favor, and am not ashamed to be punished for speaking out—I am ashamed only when my words go unheeded.

sentences.zh: 自古諫之不效，其大者身膏斧鑕，其次亦流竄四裔，其小者猶罷免終身，未有若今日不勉於聽從，亦不加於黜逐，徒餌之以無所譴嗬之恩，使皆饕富貴，甘豢養，以消靡其風節。

translations.literal: From antiquity, when remonstrance failed to take effect, at the greatest extreme the body was smeared on the axe and block; next one was exiled to the four borderlands; at the least one was dismissed and never again employed—never has there been a time like today when the court does not press for compliance yet also does not add dismissal and banishment, merely baiting men with the favor of immunity from all reproof, so that all gorge on wealth and honor, content themselves with being kept and fed, and thereby wear away their integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, when remonstrance has failed, the gravest cases ended on the executioner's block, lesser ones meant exile to the frontier, and even minor ones brought dismissal for life. Never before has there been an age like this, when the throne neither presses for compliance nor adds dismissal and exile, but only feeds officials the indulgence of going unpunished—until all gorge on rank and riches, grow content with comfortable keeping, and let their moral fiber waste away.

sentences.zh: 平居皆貪祿懷姦之士，則臨難必無仗節死義之人。

translations.literal: If in ordinary times all are men who grasp salary while harboring treachery, then in crisis there will surely be none who hold to principle and die for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: If in peaceful times the court is filled with men who draw salaries while nursing treachery, then in crisis there will be no one left to hold fast to principle and die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 陛下自夏秋以來，執政從官之死者皆不信，卒之果然乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, since summer and autumn, has disbelieved every report of death among chief administrators and attendant officials—did those deaths in the end prove true?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, since summer and autumn, has refused to believe every report that a chief minister or attendant official has died—were those deaths true in the end?

sentences.zh: 不然乎？

translations.literal: Or not?
translations.idiomatic: Or were they not?

sentences.zh: 建康趙濟死，武興吳挺死，今尚不以為然，則事有幾微於朕兆者，可諫陛下乎？

translations.literal: Zhao Ji of Jiankang died, Wu Ting of Wuxing died—if even now Your Majesty does not accept this as fact, then when matters show the faintest sign or portent, may one remonstrate with Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ji of Jiankang died; Wu Ting of Wuxing died—if Your Majesty still will not believe it, then when trouble shows the slightest warning sign, who may speak to you?

sentences.zh: 萬一變起蕭牆，禍生肘腋，陛下必將以為不信，坐受其危亡矣。

translations.literal: Should rebellion rise within the palace walls and disaster spring from one's own elbow, Your Majesty will surely treat it as unbelievable and sit by while ruin overtakes you.
translations.idiomatic: If rebellion breaks out within the palace and disaster strikes at your very side, Your Majesty will surely refuse to believe it until you sit helpless and watch the realm fall.

sentences.zh: 盜滿山東而高、斯弄權，二世不知也。

translations.literal: Bandits filled Shandong while Gao and Si manipulated power, and the Second Emperor knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits filled Shandong while Zhao Gao and Li Si manipulated power, and the Second Emperor knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 蠻寇成都而更奏捷，明皇不知也。

translations.literal: Barbarian raiders threatened Chengdu while reports of victory were submitted again and again, and Emperor Xuanzong of Tang knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raiders threatened Chengdu while repeated reports of victory were sent in, and Emperor Xuanzong knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 此猶左右聾瞽爾。

translations.literal: Those cases were merely attendants who were deaf and blind.
translations.idiomatic: In those cases the fault lay only with attendants who were deaf and blind.

sentences.zh: 今在朝之士瀝忠以告，而陛下不聽，是陛下自壅蔽其聰明也。

translations.literal: Now men at court pour out loyalty to inform Your Majesty, yet Your Majesty will not listen—this is Your Majesty blocking his own intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Now officials at court speak with loyal candor, yet Your Majesty will not listen—you are shutting off your own understanding.

sentences.zh: 今外間傳聞，以為壽皇將幸越，幸吳興，此愛陛下之深，欲泯其迹也。

translations.literal: At present outside rumor holds that Retired Emperor Shouhuang is about to visit Yue and visit Wuxing; this springs from deep love for Your Majesty and a wish to erase the traces.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor now holds that Retired Emperor Shouhuang intends to visit Yue and Wuxing—an act born of deep concern for Your Majesty and a wish to remove the cause of scandal.

sentences.zh: 陛下當亟圖所以解壽皇之憂。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty should urgently devise the means to relieve Retired Emperor Shouhuang's distress."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should act at once to relieve Retired Emperor Shouhuang's anguish."

sentences.zh: 疏入，又不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, and again there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and again no answer came.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，遷宗正寺主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong acceded, he was transferred to chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong came to the throne, Daquan was transferred to chief clerk of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 慶元元年，易太常寺主簿，遷司農寺丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingyuan his post was changed to chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingyuan he was transferred to chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 修《高宗實錄》，充檢討官。

translations.literal: He compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozong and served as revising compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He worked on the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozong as a revising compiler.

sentences.zh: 先是，韓侂胄用事，私臺諫之選為己羽翼，且欲得知名士，借其望以壓群言，一時之好進者，恨不預此選也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Tuozhou held power and privately shaped the selection of censorial and remonstrance officials into his own supporters; he also wished to obtain men of renown and borrow their prestige to suppress other voices—men eager for advancement at the time regretted only that they were not chosen for this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Tuozhou had been in power and had packed the censorial and remonstrance offices with his own partisans; he also wanted noted men whose standing might silence other opinion—careerists of the day bitterly wished they might be picked for those posts.

sentences.zh: 會御史虛位，有力薦大全者，屬大全一往見，且曰：「公朝見，除目夕下矣。

translations.literal: When the post of censor fell vacant, a powerful patron recommended Daquan, urged Daquan to pay one visit, and said: "If you attend court audience, the appointment decree will issue the same evening.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor's post fell vacant, a powerful patron recommended Daquan, urged him to pay one call, and said: "If you attend audience, the appointment will be issued that very evening.

sentences.zh: 」大全笑謝，決不往，明日遂丐外。

translations.literal: " Daquan smiled and declined, firmly refused to go, and the next day requested a provincial assignment.
translations.idiomatic: " Daquan smiled and declined; he would not go, and the next day asked to be sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 時《實錄》將上矣，上必推恩，大全去不少待。

translations.literal: At the time the Veritable Records were about to be submitted; upon submission the emperor would surely extend favor, yet Daquan departed without waiting in the least.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records were then about to be submitted, and the emperor would surely have rewarded those who compiled them—but Daquan left without waiting for that favor.

sentences.zh: 於是除知金州，至姑蘇，以病卒。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed prefect of Jinzhou; reaching Gusu, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed prefect of Jinzhou; he reached Gusu and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王信有文學，通政事。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wang Xin had literary talent and understood state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Wang Xin had literary talent and understood affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 汪大猷敦厚老成。

translations.literal: Wang Dayou was honest, generous, and seasoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dayou was honest, generous, and seasoned by experience.

sentences.zh: 袁燮學有所本。

translations.literal: Yuan Xie's learning had a solid foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie's scholarship rested on firm foundations.

sentences.zh: 吳柔勝、遊仲鴻名在偽學。

translations.literal: Wu Rousheng and You Zhonghong were listed among the proscribed Learning faction.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Rousheng and You Zhonghong were numbered among the proscribed Learning faction.

sentences.zh: 觀李祥訟趙汝愚，公論藉是以立。

translations.literal: Considering Li Xiang's defense of Zhao Ruyu, public opinion thereby found its footing.
translations.idiomatic: In Li Xiang's defense of Zhao Ruyu, one sees how public opinion found its footing.

sentences.zh: 王介、楊大全直道而行。

translations.literal: Wang Jie and Yang Daquan walked the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie and Yang Daquan held to the straight way without compromise.

sentences.zh: 宋德之其知兵者歟？

translations.literal: Was Song Dezhi one who understood warfare?
translations.idiomatic: Was Song Dezhi, then, a man who truly understood warfare?
